notes.title: Husky Assault
notes.content:
Too often have we all gazed upon the playlists and wistfully longed for the mashup of our dreams – Husky Raid and Assault. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/aaff045dab886138244a7bfffaeb9ae5bade803e.jpg[/img]

Today, our dreams come true. We’re mixing the bombastic chaos of Husky Raid with the strategy of tactical Assault. We call it…Husky Assault. [i](Betcha didn’t see that coming.[/i])

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Assault on the Husky Raid[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/e8adcc15955d7c89d2b61c42c120cfa37eaa3dbe.jpg[/img]

The linear and somewhat claustrophobic nature of Husky Raid makes for thrilling and exciting games of Capture the Flag. That action gets flipped head over heels with the introduction of Assault. Now you’ll have to work together as a team to battle for the (neutral) bomb then escort your carrier to the base and allow them to plant the bomb… drive a wedge through the enemy lines, and try not to get left behind as the intensity of  Husky Raid rages all around you.

A new map is also joining the pantheon of tried-and-true Husky Raids:

[h3]Warehouse[/h3]
Credits: Karmaplex1283, ADSR7865
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/a45096d8-7feb-4739-b67f-3b13781e32d1]Bookmark[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/d8d1762e02b4668cea2c77d24ca85b29aa7dc041.jpg[/img]

Get your grunge on – a certain pro skater would feel right at home in this warehouse skate park.

[hr][/hr]
Husky Assault is there – what are you waiting for? Drop in and launch your assault on the enemy now!

tags.feature: Today, our dreams come true. We’re mixing the bombastic chaos of Husky Raid with the strategy of tactical Assault. We call it…Husky Assault.
A new map is also joining the pantheon of tried-and-true Husky Raids:

notes.title: Operation: Forerunner
notes.content:
It’s time to reclaim what was lost. Fight for the grace of the Mantle in Operation: Forerunner, live now through May 6.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/cecb4b2be750c7cd77a4277fe83ab8bd0229d60c.jpg[/img]

Once the galaxy’s self-appointed caretakers, the Forerunners have left behind many secrets in the form of sacred rings, colossal installations, mysterious artifacts—and devastating military technology.

The latest free 20-tier Operation Pass offers a chance to reclaim the Prefect armor from the annals of history. Reverse-engineered from the combat skin of the Forerunner Prefect class, this fan-favorite Halo 4 armor set has been adapted and reforged for a new chapter in Spartan excellence.

Complete all 20 tiers to prove yourself worthy of the title. May your foes tremble before you!

[previewyoutube=vGov5ZzWrYE;full][/previewyoutube]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]New Mode: Husky Assault[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/9e658cb201d380265fbfde6bf431f2352d274251.jpg[/img]

Strategy, meet chaos. [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1240440/announcements/detail/514080375518004497]Husky Assault[/url] combines the do-or-die rush of [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1240440/announcements/detail/3647406545972440190]Husky Raid[/url] with the tactical objectives of [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1240440/announcements/detail/525333670813238285]Assault[/url]. Weapons are random, options are few, and you’ve got to wrestle the bomb from the enemy’s clutches by any means necessary.

With nowhere to go but forward, you’ll have to adapt your methods on the fly—or suffer the consequences.

[h3]New Map: Warehouse[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/15ab57d650b323173d3273d2f7faee05bd8fa54d.jpg[/img]

Credits: Karmaplex1283, ADSR785 
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/a45096d8-7feb-4739-b67f-3b13781e32d1]Bookmark[/url] 

Warehouse has been added to the map rotation in Husky Assault and Husky Raid modes. A concrete paradise laden with gloomy sunbeams, hellish half-pipes, and just the right amount of grunge, this map proves that skate parks really [i]are[/i] dangerous. Good thing you wore a helmet.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]New Mode: Ranked 1v1 Showdown[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/ce3d01f3b12017b86954e1767194f9958fb577c8.jpg[/img]

We’ve added Ranked 1v1 Showdown to [i]Halo Infinite[/i] as a new Ranked rotational playlist! Just like in the social version, you and one opponent will compete on a slice of fan-favorite [i]Halo[/i] maps with new starting weapons in every round.

In the Ranked version of 1v1 Showdown, starting weapons have been tailored for a more competitive experience, focusing primarily on precision weapons to give players a true test of aim, strategy, and composure.

Join us April 18–20 for the kickoff of the HCS Season at [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/news/optic-major]HCS Major Arlington[/url], where players and fans will be able to compete using the Ranked 1v1 Showdown mode for a chance to claim prizes from a $5,000 prize pool. Better get practicing!

[h2]Coming Soon: BTB Maps & Modes[/h2]

We’ll soon refresh the Big Team Battle playlist and add two new modes to [i]Halo Infinite[/i]’s multiplayer mythos. Jump in later this Operation to test your mettle in BTB Extraction and BTB Assault! More details on the new modes below.

Stay tuned for a full writeup of the upcoming BTB playlist updates, including info on four new maps arriving in the BTB map rotation.

[h3]BTB Extraction[/h3]

BTB Extraction introduces multi-site Extraction for up to 24 players. With two target zones active at a time, your team will need to secure extraction sites, deploy the beacons, and defend your turf long enough to score.

Seven points to win and twice the exposed flank? Perfect conditions for glory.

[h3]BTB Assault[/h3]

In BTB Assault, teams of up to 12 players face off in the classic strategic bomber mode, where seconds make the difference between Spartans and smithereens. Whether you’re fending off would-be sappers or sneaking behind their lines, bringing the boom just got a little bit harder.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Operation Pass[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/b8b87d728f76909b18f03f28174eed15a70ca7c2.jpg[/img]

The Forerunners have returned. This Operation Pass promises triumphant Spartans the enameled excellence of the Prefect armor, the coveted battle regalia of an ancient caste. Those who walk the path of the Forerunners can also unlock the Sorvad Solid emblem and the Odin’s Eye helmet attachment.

Complete this Operation’s reward tiers by May 6 to unlock the full armor set. Once an Operation has concluded, all customization rewards offered in its free reward tiers will eventually make their way to The Exchange in a future Operation—but cataloging specimens like these can take time.

[h3]Premium Pass[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/43ef03c0c22aa60c852ffe9cde1daf56a535587c.jpg[/img]

Secure a Premium Pass to lock in your Operation: Forerunner rewards and complete them at your leisure. Premium Pass holders will also instantly unlock the Promethean Assault Rifle MA40 weapon model and the Steel Fall weapon coating, plus bonus XP and an additional challenge slot. 

[i]Once purchased, a Premium Operation Pass never expires and its reward tiers can be completed at your leisure. Premium Operation Passes are only available while their respective Operation is active. The Premium Pass for Operation: Forerunner is available to purchase now through May 6. Premium customization rewards offered in this Premium Pass will be added to The Shop to purchase separately at a later date.[/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Free Unlock: Women's History Month Bundle[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/1cda1cdf027ac64a8c88d6e9f1de8cfc4ab13a10.jpg[/img]

If you missed your chance to claim last month’s free log-in unlock, the Women’s History Month Bundle can now be found in the Customization Menu. Simply select any WHM item within the Armor Hall to acquire the full bundle, featuring the Women’s History Month armor coating, visor, nameplate, and emblems.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Fuel Rod SPNKr[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/673d63f248040adb57f36ba6936ddc05d182d8c4.jpg[/img]

The Fuel Rod SPNKr is an unholy alliance between UNSC technology and Banished ingenuity. Modified to fire fuel rod munitions, this new take on a Covenant classic is available as a power weapon on maps and can be spawned in Forge. Six shots from this rowdy rod-thrower should give ‘em something to think about.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Waypoint Chronicle[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/d5924929317e9466d8f01d3ed05ddd579d377918.jpg[/img]

Along with this Operation comes a new Waypoint Chronicle, releasing April 10.

Study of the Forerunners in recent years has unlocked revelations about humanity’s own far-reaching past.

Once an interstellar empire and rival to the Forerunners, these civilizations were at the center of events that would shape the future of the galaxy through the emergence of the virulent, all-consuming parasite known as the Flood.

But as research by ONI is conducted on a derelict cruiser belonging to the ancient human Ancestors, strange effects begin to take hold of the crew.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Shop[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/42e7fb8db75f15355275276118398b9e0f73d0d6.png[/img]

Champions should wear something that says, “My singular valor must be preserved and studied.” Purchase the Promethean Reclamation bundle to unlock two new armor sets from the [i]Halo[/i] legendarium.

Harkening to the ascendancy of the Didact and his Warrior-Servants, the Sundered Star and Vindicator armor sets are the perfect attire for scattering one’s enemies to cosmic dust, especially with the Promethean Commando weapon model in your fearsome grip.

This bundle also includes the Composition kill effect set so you can catalog your foes for posterity with complete disintegration. Probably a good time for pithy remarks about their hubris while you’re at it.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]The Exchange[/h2]

[i]Earn Spartan Points by playing multiplayer matches and completing weekly challenges in Halo Infinite. Use your Spartan Points to claim armor customizations, weapon models, emblems, and effects at The Exchange.[/i]

In Operation: Forerunner, we’re featuring Forerunner-inspired armor and a “back catalog” of retro-inspired designs from the Cyber Showdown Event. Embrace the digital revolution with the new UA/Prefect Buckler, or prove you’re with the band by unlocking the Craig Cover Band stance, the Halo VHS weapon charm, and more!

notes.title: Firefight Classic
notes.content:
Welcome back to Firefight! The classic Firefight experience returns to [i]Halo Infinite[/i], alongside the King of the Hill variant. Dropping out of slipspace in tandem with the launch of Operation: Blue Team, the PvE fight begins come March 11.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/a0cc307b756bc4f1ca35802cfb6eab514286eed9.jpg[/img]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Firefight Through Time[/h2]

Firefight was first introduced way back in 2009 with [i]Halo 3: ODST[/i]. You and up to three of your buddies could squad up and put your skills to the test surviving round after round of Covenant hordes attacking your position.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/acb444bdeba4f4a1dbadef4c18f2e007e380177b.jpg[/img]

Through the years, Firefight has seen various iterations and has evolved in many ways. In [i]Halo: Reach[/i], you had armor abilities and additional customization. [i]Halo 5[/i] saw the introduction of Warzone Firefight that pitted a team of eight against Covenant and Promethean forces. Even [i]Halo Wars 2[/i] brought in a tower defense-inspired variant, Terminus Firefight.

The latest, [i]Halo Infinite[/i]’s Firefight: King of the Hill, has you and your squad capturing and defending hills against incoming Banished forces.

But now it’s time to return to the classic.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Current Objective: Survive[/h2]

It’s the formula we all know and love. You and three squadmates versus the endless waves of enemies with one thing running through your mind:

[i]Survive[/i].

In KOTH, it’s easy to know when you’ve won or lost because you are either in the hill at the end of the round, or not (or MIA I suppose), but Classic comes with [b]waves[/b], [b]rounds[/b], and [b]sets[/b]. Let’s break it down.

[list]
[*] One [b]Round[/b] is comprised of five [b]Waves[/b] of enemies
[list][*] Wave 1 is an easy wave
[*] Waves 2-4 are mid-tier difficulties
[*] Wave 5 is a boss round[/list][*]Three Rounds (plus a Bonus Round) comprise a Set
[list][*] This is a total of 15 waves[/list][/list]

Did we mention this mode is endless? The game keeps going as long as you keep surviving so stock up on snacks and water if you’re in this for the long haul.

Bonus rounds are little mini-breaks between sets. All Skulls are on, enemies are on Easy mode, no lives are lost, and the stakes are low. And speaking of the stakes, let’s talk lives.

[h2]I Will Survive[/h2]

At the start of each match, you’ll have [b]7 lives[/b] in your team’s life pool. These are shared amongst the four of you, so if someone is charging forward willy-nilly you’ll quickly find yourself looking at the Post-Game Carnage Report. If you play well and stay alive, you’ll preserve your life pool for the later, harder rounds.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/4cfec622d5d122fa7f767ae3db68777ccee9d50a.jpg[/img]

But sometimes, deaths happen—we’ve all been there. At the end of each set your team will earn an extra life. Additionally, you’ll gain a life for each 1,000 points earned during the bonus round. So if you turn around and find yourself face to face with a Grunt rushing you with plasma grenades, don’t sweat it too much – you can always make it up later.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]We Need to Evac[/h2]

New to [i]Halo Infinite[/i], you’ll now be able to choose to end your match at the end of a set. Before the next round begins, you’ll see a zone pop up that says, “Complete the mission.” If at least two of you hop into the zone, you’ll be extracted from the mission and the match will end. If you don’t get in the zone before the next round, you’ll be committed until you either:
[list][*] Run out of lives
[*] Make it to the end of the next set[/list]
If you’ve survived, congratulations! The next round is about to begin. Each set has a new set of Skulls that will activate. You’ll see a new Skull activate on rounds two and three, adding an extra layer of difficulty to the firefight.

If you’re running low on ammo, don’t fret—you’ll get a resupply between each round.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]The Maps[/h2]

You can bookmark the mode created by Artifice7285 here:

[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/modes/d7f4a252-5741-4f02-aba0-93c022032d9a]Firefight Classic[/url]

And then grab the maps you’ll be playing on below!

[h3]Alpha Site[/h3]
Credits: Its L0L0, LudoHT, MikRips, Mr Greencastle
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/42fb7640-19f0-477f-b202-4314acb4b0e3]Bookmark[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/23bbb4603972c19c503d1b8c73f404736cee8949.jpg[/img]

Many a Vidmaster: Endure achievement was earned within these hallowed halls on the Road to Recon.

[h3]Courtyard[/h3]
Credits: bullet2thehead9, Mr Greencastle
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/2f337095-3c19-4fb8-96ec-d9321c015655]Bookmark[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/654a6415832fe47470570987b8014066fdd58e07.jpg[/img]

We’ve got Jackals in the Courtyard!

[h3]Forest Firefight[/h3]
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/841242db-013f-4b10-871e-c432379e852c]Bookmark[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/deda7d92d388382ace1eddeddc7a0d687dc9abe0.jpg[/img]

Only you can prevent forest fires.

[h3]House of Reckoning[/h3]
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/f6fba25d-1ce2-4645-9b7c-feae89a576f7]Bookmark[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/91e747e5196537e721dee3ab3f5b2a83e8164d32.jpg[/img]

Do you reckon anyone’s home?

[h3]Security Zone[/h3]
Credits: Its L0L0, LudoHT, MikRips, Cousin Tim, VIrus11010, ArtN00b, Mr Greencastle
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/96ede14f-623e-4868-a745-e791d3dd8e31]Bookmark[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/e54bd9d2887a282eda43d08a751328928d24e365.jpg[/img]

Perhaps the most quintessential map from Halo 3: ODST returns so secure those zones.

[hr][/hr]
We’re very excited to have this mode available in matchmaking and we know you are looking forward to jumping in. How long you survive the waves of enemies is up to you. 

Play smart, help each other out, and watch those lives!

notes.title: Hot Swap
notes.content:
For those that have played Fiescalation in MCC or other gun games in another popular shooter, Hot Swap should be fairly familiar. If not, it’s okay—we got you covered!

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Swap It Like It's Hot[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/b027063ffa72ac0ca31716b35bab65781d631c84.jpg[/img]

Overall, this is a very straightforward and simple mode. It’s your team vs the enemy team and everyone has the same weapons and equipment. Yes, everyone. In other versions of this mode, you often find your weapons/loadouts advancing to the next tier after each kill but in Hot Swap, you’ll keep those loadouts for 30 seconds at a time. After that, the proverbial dice are rolled and everyone is gifted a new combo. Hone your skill and stay flexible – things can change on a dime.

Here are the set loadouts you should be prepared to work with at any given moment:

While you may see a repeat loadout, it won’t happen until you’ve cycled through the entire list. Also if you are mid-grapple when things swap, you might find yourself saying, “wow I flew pretty good for a brick!” as your grapple disappears midway through. Good luck.

[hr][/hr]
You’ll be playing on a variety of current Arena maps that should be familiar but there is one new map to check out:

Focus on the enemy, don’t let the map’s edges become your nemesis.

[hr][/hr]
Hot Swap is available in matchmaking right now so jump in while it's hot and see what you get!

notes.title: March Playlist Update
notes.content:
When Operation: Blue Team comes to [i]Halo Infinite[/i] next week, it’ll include a hefty playlist update. We’ll be consolidating some things for Match Composer and adding some new experiences that we think you’ll be pleased with as well. Let’s get into things!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/9c1e52b591b834b925d063d46439cd39e35d72f2.jpg[/img]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Match Composer[/h2]

As [i]Halo Infinite[/i] has evolved, the Infinite team has worked hard to bring a ton of new experiences to the game: Husky Raid, Fiesta Castle Wars, Action Sack, Firefight, Infection, BTB Sentry Defense, and so many more. As a result, there are now a whole lotta options for you to choose from in the Match Composer. (The options are not quite [i]infinite[/i] but pretty close!) We’ve monitored the data and seen what is being selected or searched for most often and we’ve been closely evaluating the health of the various playlists.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/b100ac615b187445127cc55f9f7187e30997b0d9.jpg[/img]

At the same time, we’ve also heard your feedback that some of the current Match Composer lists are a bit confusing and not as coherent as they could be. With this in mind, and with spring on the horizon, we’re taking this opportunity to do a bit of spring cleaning: specifically tightening up and re-arranging part of the Match Composer.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Q&A With the Infinite Team[/h2]

There’s a lot coming with this update so we sat down with the Infinite team and chatted a bit about the upcoming changes.

[b]What are the ultimate goals for playlist health overall?[/b]

[i]The ultimate goal for all playlists is striking a balance between low match times and solid match quality with the least amount of skill discrepancy between the two teams as possible. We want players to go into matches to have fun and get in those matches fast so trying to balance the two is always a delicate dance.

With Match Composer, players have more freedom and flexibility to choose how they play Halo matchmaking than ever before. We’re seeing players take advantage of that across the board which we love to see. The downside to the Match Composer, however, is that it’s entirely possible to choose too narrow of a search resulting in really long search times to find a match.[/i]

[b]What are some ways you go about ensuring players can get those “good matches” of short queues and teams with low skill discrepancy?[/b]

[i]We started by looking at all the playlists available to players today in the Match Composer and there are a lot! There are nine social playlists with over 100 modes across the various lists…28 in Rumble Pit alone. Even within a single playlist, there are many, many different ways for players to “silo” (aka create a search so narrow that the time to match is very long) themselves via their search parameters. We also took a look at the options across different playlists and have heard your feedback of, “This doesn’t make sense here, it should be over there.”

The goal with this update is to reduce the number of silos by working to group like content with like. When we look at Action Sack, we agree that that’s the logical home for some of the more wacky or party modes just like we agree that “Arena Objective” is probably not the best home for Team Snipers.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/6233ce4b5338fa84bc6d036553f4c2c5ae0e8d9e.jpg[/img]

[b]How do you identify the problem areas and how do you know where to focus your efforts when working on things?[/b]

[i]So our first stop when it comes to checking playlist health/data is the analytics team. We can see what silos players are choosing, how popular a specific silo is (or isn’t), and we can see that across each playlist. So from Quick Play to Action Sack, we can see what modes players are gravitating towards versus what isn’t resonating as well.

If we look at Rumble Pit as an example (remember it has 28 separate modes in the playlist itself!), here are the top 5 most searched modes (note: these are all FFA variants):
[list][*] Community Shotty Snipes
[*] Fiesta Slayer
[*] Ninja Slayer
[*] Shotty Snipes
[*] Slayer[/list]
From the information we gather based on your selections and playtime, we can see that players in Rumble Pit prefer the more “serious” game modes available to them so moving ones that feel out of place, such as FFA Purple Reign and Kong Slayer, to a more appropriate playlist, like Action Sack, just makes a lot of sense.

We’ve also observed that when players are wanting to play Shotty Snipers, for example, they select both versions available – Shotty Snipers and Community Shotty Snipers. To help limit the silos available, we’re combining the Community modes with the studio modes into one.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/a2cc9adce2349eb4883dba50ffd2a3bdeeeb62c9.jpg[/img]

[i]Another good example to look at is Quick Play. There’s currently 20 different modes in the playlist and with the top modes being:
[list][*] Fiesta
[*] Husky Raid
[*] Super Fiesta
[*] Super Husky Raid
[*] Team Slayer[/list]
The silos at the bottom are incredibly narrow and aren’t resulting in many matches as a whole in their current state. We recognize those are fun and unique modes so we’re looking to move them to other playlists where they will hopefully be more thematically fitting.[/i]

[b]You have been putting out a lot of new playlists recently. Is there anything fun you can tease about what’s coming?[/b]

[i]We’ve been really working hard on the combination of new and refreshed experiences to bring to the game. We don’t want to spoil what’s on the horizon but we do have a few exciting modes coming soon! Maybe as soon as Tuesday…[/i]

[hr][/hr]

A huge thank you to the team for all their hard work!

We’re looking for ward to what’s coming next but, in the meantime, here’s a breakdown of what you can find in the various playlists after next week’s update.

notes.title: Operation: Blue Team
notes.content:
Welcome to Blue Team, Spartans.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/080b9f5204909f41738fa443563345f0da050644.jpg[/img]

This legendary Spartan-II team has a prodigious combat record spanning well over two hundred military operations against all kinds of foes—from the colonial insurrection to the Covenant, and the many threats that have arisen in recent years.

While John-117, Fred-104, Kelly-087, and Linda-058 have typically been the primary members of Blue Team, the roster has evolved over time—and now it is time for you to join them.

[previewyoutube=8A_SBMoeezc;full][/previewyoutube]

Operation: Blue Team is live from March 11 to April 8, let’s explore what’s new!

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Firefight Classic[/h2]

Bip, bap, bam! Classic Firefight returns in Operation: Blue Team.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/acb444bdeba4f4a1dbadef4c18f2e007e380177b.jpg[/img]

You know the drill. Each new wave brings progressively more difficult Banished bad guys—five waves make up a round, three rounds (plus a bonus round) make a set. You can keep the party going for as long as you want. No, really, you could keep the good times rolling with your squad into next week if you really wanted to! Or—at the end of a set—head to the exfiltration zone and end the match.

Try not to die, as lives are limited, but you’ll be able to earn them back by successfully completing a bonus round.

Of course, a classic mode pairs nicely with some classic maps! Return to ONI’s headquarters in New Mombasa as Alpha Site and Security Zone from [i]Halo 3: ODST[/i] return, along with SWORD Base’s Courtyard from [i]Halo: Reach[/i].

For more details, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1240440/view/547854839202187312]check out our Firefight Classic playlist blog[/url].

Next wave’s coming in. Get ready, Spartans!

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Hot Swap[/h2]

A Spartan must be prepared for anything—a sharpened tool able to react to any situation on the battlefield.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/4ee543ced6d40c48f3023bda7ded1e090168afd1.jpg[/img]

Hot Swap puts that to the ultimate test, as this team-based 4v4 mode switches up everybody’s loadout every thirty seconds—that means you, your teammates, and the enemy team. Maybe you’ll all get a rocket launcher, maybe you’ll get a plasma pistol. Whatever the situation you’ll have to adjust your role and strategy if you and your team mean to claim victory.

It’s long been said that Halo’s gameplay is built on the foundation of cycling “thirty seconds of fun,” and that is what you will find at the heart of Hot Swap.

For the full debrief, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1240440/view/547854839202187314]head to our Hot Swap playlist blog[/url].

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Operation Pass[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/61b6f423842b0ae50ea36e242c719d4f1150a722.jpg[/img]

Front and center of this Operation Pass is Kelly-087, the fastest Spartan.

Exceptionally talented at reconnaissance and close-quarters combat, Kelly is known for her lightning-fast reflexes and ability to run at speeds of 40mph for extended periods. Recently, this killer queen has also developed a fondness for what is considered “classical” music in the 26th century.

Acquire Kelly-087's HERMES-class Mjolnir armor in the free 20-tier Operation Pass. The free pass is available to acquire and progress until the next Operation arrives on April 8. If you miss out or don't complete it before it rotates out, fret not - all of the free customization content will be available to acquire via Spartan Points in the Exchange at a later date.

Upgrade to the Premium Pass to acquire the Wintergeist armor coating to round out Kelly’s look. The Premium Pass comes with an additional Challenge Slot, bonus XP, and never expires. The Blue Team Premium Pass is available for purchase until April 8. Once purchased, it's yours to progress and complete at your leisure with no expiration. If you miss out on purchasing it before it rotates out, the Wintergeist armor coating will be available for purchase in the Shop at a later date.

[i]Update March 13: This section has been edited for clarity regarding the status of the Free and Premium Operation Pass once the next Operation launches on April 8.[/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Waypoint Chronicle[/h2]

Blue Team have arrived and they’re bringing with them a new Waypoint Chronicle!

Set in September 2559, just weeks before the events of Troy Denning’s novel [i]Halo: Shadows of Reach[/i], this Waypoint Chronicle takes place at the planet and space station seen in [i]Halo Infinite[/i]’s “Step Inside” trailer as the GEN3 Mjolnir armor is completed.

“[i]September 2559. As the UNSC Infinity’s crew prepare to return to Reach for Operation: WOLFE, the legendary Spartans of Blue Team field test their GEN3 Mjolnir armor alongside ODSTs of the Ninth Platoon[/i].”

[b]COMING MARCH 12[/b]
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Free Unlock: Black History Month Bundle[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/ccd5814870a467f3f808c30c88e7ce1775820346.png[/img]

Missed your chance to claim last month’s log-in unlock? The Black History Month Bundle can now be obtained for free in the Customization Menu. Simply select any Black History Month item within the Armor Hall to acquire the full bundle, featuring the Black History Month Armor Coating, Visor, and multiple Emblem sets.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]The Exchange[/h2]

A new Operation means a refresh of The Exchange!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/6287a9d005b08e6bdb23acf822d70a48eac5b7de.jpg[/img]

Play matches and complete weekly challenges to earn Spartan Points which you can spend in The Exchange.

This Operation, EAGLESTRIKE fans can acquire some classics from the Entrenched events, such as the Kerberos helmet, Wizard Pockets chest attachment, and more. And, in celebration of St. Patrick’s Day, some new themed emblems can be acquired to mark the occasion.

[h2Shop[/h2]

Start off the Spartan-II reunion tour with the Blue Team bundle!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/79e79b8f1ba1711f8826af7202e3ed3d1f3d9c80.png[/img]

This bundle includes Linda-058’s Argus set, Master Chief’s Mark VI MOD [GEN2] armor, and Frederic-104’s Cohort ensemble. Also included is the legendary Nornfang sniper rifle, Inferno Bandit, Wyrd Aura mythic FX, and a pallet-load of legendary armor customization pieces and coatings. Finish out the team with Kelly-087’s gear as part of the Operation Pass!

Recreate your favorite member of Blue Team or mix ‘n’ match the armor to your heart’s content.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]See Something, Say Something[/h2]

To read the full patch notes for today's Operation update, [url=https://aka.ms/HaloInfiniteUpdate]head over to the Halo Support site[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/3b707e1df15de2d0c0080759c6f0819b6bc2321e.jpg[/img]

You can submit tickets on a wide range of topics that include reports of Audio Issues, Crashes, Game Save Corruption, Report a Player, General Bug Reports, and more.

notes.title: Assault
notes.content:
Defend your base – Assault arrives in [i]Halo Infinite[/i]! First introduced in [i]Halo 2[/i], this mode is the reverse of Capture the Flag. Rather than getting into your opponent’s base and stealing their flag, you’re sneaking into their base with a bomb, attempting to plant it. It’s totally identical, just in reverse.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Bomb Armed[/h2]
Assault comes in multiple flavors and the two being introduced with Operation: Frontlines are:
[list][*] One Bomb
[*] Neutral Bomb[/list]
Some of you might be wondering… “What’s the difference?” Thank you for asking!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/4aadd0e8b0017783553394be67207dca5c698535.jpg[/img]

Neutral Bomb starts with the bomb in a neutral position on the map (usually the middle) and each team fights for control of the bomb. Once you have the explosive in your possession, your objective is to infiltrate the enemy base and plant it.

One Bomb is a one-sided objective mode that alternates with each team taking turns being on offense and defense. If you’re on offense, the bomb will spawn in your zone and it’s up to your team to mount the assault on the enemy’s base. If you are on defense, your goal is preventing that bomb from being planted in your area.

Those of you that played [i]Halo 2/3[/i] know that One Bomb on Zanzibar/Last Resort was the classic One Bomb experience. So classic that we’ve got not just 4v4 Assault available, but also Squad Battle Assault pitting 8v8 in the battle of the bomb! After all, Assault is not only a really great 4v4 objective mode, it also plays very well in larger teams.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]The 4v4 Battlegrounds[/h2]

Some of these maps should tickle the nostalgia bone. You can bookmark the modes here:
[list][*] [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/modes/92862008-3369-43b6-96e7-ef80f610cdc1]Neutral Bomb Assault[/url]
[*] [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/modes/43c5f35e-1af0-4155-b9d9-cae03858c180]One Bomb Assault[/url][/list]
 …and then grab the maps below!

A mashup with some familiar [i]Halo 2 [/i] (Sanctuary) and [i]Halo 3[/i] (Guardian) map feels, you’ll feel like you’re right at home on Delta Halo.

[h3]Aquarius[/h3]

The grass isn’t always greener but the hydroponics sure make the scenery nice and verdant.

One misstep could be the catalyst you need to swing the outcome in your favor.

The battle for the castle will happen on this map with a beautiful vista to take in as you watch for the bomb.

tags.feature: Defend your base – Assault arrives in [i]Halo Infinite[/i]! First introduced in [i]Halo 2[/i], this mode is the reverse of Capture the Flag.
Assault comes in multiple flavors and the two being introduced with Operation: Frontlines are: [list][*] One Bomb [*] Neutral Bomb[/list]
Neutral Bomb starts with the bomb in a neutral position on the map (usually the middle) and each team fights for control of the bomb.
One Bomb is a one-sided objective mode that alternates with each team taking turns being on offense and defense.
So classic that we’ve got not just 4v4 Assault available, but also Squad Battle Assault pitting 8v8 in the battle of the bomb!
The Infection playlist is being added to Action Sack and Castle Wars is being added to Squad Battle.

notes.title: Operation: Frontlines | Spring Update 2025
notes.content:
Touchdown, hit it marines! The 2025 Spring Update for [i]Halo Infinite[/i] begins with Operation: Frontlines.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/598a4c7151a31d278efff1c228b8e7591f0ceaa0.jpg[/img]

Get your gauntleted hands on the Fuel Rod SPNKr, a new weapon for [i]Halo Infinite[/i] based on an old Covenant favorite—now repurposed by the Banished.

Fashion your Spartan with the finest flair in the brand-new Operation Pass, a vastly expanded offering for the first Operation of each major Update that now brings 50 tiers of customization rewards. Give the enemy team back their bomb as the classic Assault mode returns, and that’s just the tip of the iceberg…

[previewyoutube=_1mMLLeao58;full][/previewyoutube]

Let’s dive into what’s live in [i]Halo Infinite[/i] today with the arrival of Operation: Frontlines.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Fuel Rod SPNKr[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/673d63f248040adb57f36ba6936ddc05d182d8c4.jpg[/img]

It’s not just old Covenant technology that the Banished ravenously repurpose and reforge into their own tools of domination, but the UNSC’s as well.

Introducing the Fuel Rod SPNKr, a rocket launcher that has been heavily modified by the Banished and fires Venezian-repackaged fuel rod munitions.

The Fuel Rod SPNKr works great against vehicles—its six-shot magazine makes it effective against a wide range of targets.

You will be able to find the Fuel Rod SPNKr as a power weapon on maps, but if you want to get to grips with this new take on a Covenant classic you can jump into the Academy’s Training mode—or spawn it in Forge for some custom games.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Operation Pass[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/de31fbdacd08c26e86af8a87195ccec08ce77c58.jpg[/img]

[i]Halo Infinite[/i]’s Operation Pass has evolved!

After tracking community feedback about Operation Passes over the last year, we are exploring a new format for players to earn more customization goodness for even more value.

For the first Operation of each Update, there will be an expanded Premium Operation Pass which contains [u][b]50 tiers[/b][/u] of rewards and [u][b]four full armor sets[/b][/u].

For the following two Operations in an Update, the Operation Passes will be the traditional 20-tier offering that players experienced in 2024.

[h3]Free Pass[/h3]

As before, if you’ve been enjoying the free Operation Pass, your experience is largely unchanged. During the time the Operation is live, you will be able to earn 20 tiers of free rewards, including one full armor set.

[h3]Premium Pass[/h3]

The price of the Premium Operation Pass has been slightly adjusted for this offering as it’s been expanded from 20 to 50 tiers, and from one complete armor set to four, providing the following options:
[list][*] [b]1,000 Credits[/b]: The Operation Pass is durable, offers bonus XP, provides an extra Challenge slot, and immediately gives you multiple bonus items. Provides the ability to earn four full armor sets.
[*] [b]2,500 Credits[/b]: All of the above, and instantly unlocks the first 20 levels out of 50.[/list]
The Premium Pass is only available for purchase during the time the Operation is live, and will no longer be available for purchase once that month-long window has closed. If you miss out on purchasing any Premium Operation Pass going forward but want the customization content it offered, you will be able to find it in the Shop at a later date (and at an adjusted price).

Likewise, the armor set from the Free Pass will flow into The Exchange and return at a later date where players will be able to acquire that armor with Spartan Points (earned simply by completing matches).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/a358161d3cde8cce56511044a1409f2210edae36.jpg[/img]

For a full breakdown on all the details of the new Operation Pass format, be sure to [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1240440/announcements/detail/525333670813237830]check out our Spring Update blog[/url]!

Secure the Premium Pass for access to all 50 tiers and instantly unlock the BR75A2 Hammer weapon model for the BR75 Battle Rifle, Xenothreat weapon coating, Sequence Assembly weapon charm, and Pattern Seeker visor.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Mode: Assault[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/9c1e52b591b834b925d063d46439cd39e35d72f2.jpg[/img]

The Assault mode—a fan-favorite since [i]Halo 2[/i]—is en route to [i]Halo Infinite[/i]!

Each team defends their bomb site as they battle over a neutral bomb in the center of the map, aiming to escort the intrepid and heroic bomb carrier to the enemy base to arm and detonate it.

Of course, Assault is a mode that comes with multiple variants as well. When it arrives with the Spring Update, you’ll be able to play both Neutral Bomb and One Bomb.

For more information on this returning mode, [url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1240440/announcements/detail/525333670813238285]head over to our Assault Playlist blog[/url]!

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Additonal Updates[/h2]



As the first Operation of the Spring Update, there’s a whole lot more that has come with Frontlines!

Sandbox updates have tuned various weapons and grenades, as well as movement; the Ranked experience has been refreshed, bringing some changes to existing maps along with the return of [i]Halo 5[/i]’s fan-favorite Coliseum; and Forge has received some updates as well.

[url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1240440/announcements/detail/525333670813237830]Jump into our Spring Update blog for all the details[/url]!

[hr][/hr]
[h2]The Exchange[/h2]

The Exchange has been refreshed and contains various customization rewards for players to acquire with Spartan Points.

It’s February, which means that Valentine’s Day is just around the corner! You’ll find some lovely new emblems themed around the occasion along with returning items from the Interference Event which was all about decking out your RAKSHASA armor.

A little something for those that like to keep the Spartan wardrobe fresh.

[h3]ODST Special Issue[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/8a2fdaa03582e5ac4a83cedee0639ea183f49335.jpg[/img]

Feet first into the fire! Be the first to field test the new Trooper and ODST Hardshell sets, Helljumper-themed armor accessories, SOCOM-issue Sidekick Automag, and combat tested coatings for your armor and weapons!

Secure this super-sized bundle to additionally acquire the bonus Battle Cross Death FX.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/09d8dc691738a6a75a41ec5581e013631704a8aa.jpg[/img]

notes.title: 2025 Spring Update
notes.content:
The Spring Update for [i]Halo Infinite[/i] is on its way!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/630661770e4438d96ea85eaa8d296a5634404ed2.jpg[/img]

When Operation: Frontlines kicks off the Spring Update at the start of February, you’ll be getting your hands on a new weapon (a new take on an old favorite), an overhauled and expanded premium Operation Pass with four unique sets of armor to acquire, the return of the fan-favorite Assault mode, balance updates, and much more.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Updates & Operations[/h2]

As a reminder, [i]Halo Infinite[/i] has a new update format.

At the end of last year, we released the Winter Update from November 2024 through January 2025, which included Operation: Great Journey (November), Operation: Snowbound (December), and Operation: Brute Force (January).

The 2025 Spring Update for [i]Halo Infinite[/i] has the same format—three new Operations are on the way, starting with Operation: Frontlines on February 4.

Here’s how the update format works: Since the first Operation is paired with the launch of an Update (in this case, the 2025 Spring Update kicks off with Operation: Frontlines), it will contain a larger offering of content. This is where you can expect a Spartan-sized delivery of things like a new sandbox weapon, new modes, and so on, while the next two Operations will offer smaller updates.

So, what upcoming Operations have you got to look forward to in the Spring Update?
[list][*] [b]Operation: Frontlines[/b] (February 4)
[*] [b]Operation: Blue Team[/b] (March 11)
[*] [b]Operation: Forerunner[/b] (April 8)[/list]
And then, looking even further ahead, once Operation: Forerunner wraps up, we’ll have the next “seasonal” release with the [i]Halo Infinite[/i] Summer Update and three new Operations. We’ll have more details to share on what that entails at a later date.
[hr][/hr]
[h2]New Weapon: Fuel Rod SPNKr[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/673d63f248040adb57f36ba6936ddc05d182d8c4.jpg[/img]

It’s not just old Covenant technology that the Banished ravenously repurpose and reforge into their own tools of domination, but the UNSC’s as well.

Introducing the Fuel Rod SPNKr, a rocket launcher that has been heavily modified by the Banished and fires Venezian-repackaged fuel rod munitions.

The Fuel Rod SPNKr works great against vehicles—its six-shot magazine makes it effective against a wide range of targets.

You will be able to find the Fuel Rod SPNKr as a power weapon on maps, but if you want to get to grips with this new take on a Covenant classic you can jump into the Academy’s Training mode—or spawn it in Forge for some custom games.

As noted in the above section, the first Operation in each major Update offers heftier additions like new sandbox weapons. As we look ahead, we can indeed confirm that the Mutilator—a Banished-themed shotgun—is actively being worked on by the team and is targeting the Summer Update.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Operation Pass[/h2]

[i]Halo Infinite[/i]’s Operation Pass is evolving.

We have been listening to and tracking community feedback about [i]Halo Infinite[/i]’s Operation releases over the last year, as we are looking to improve this experience for players.

Thus far, each Operation Pass has offered 20 tiers of rewards, typically including a themed set of armor, additional customization elements (such as emblems), Spartan Points to spend in The Exchange, and bonus items for those who purchase the Pass.

This year, we want to expand our offering to players, so here’s what you can expect to see when Operation: Frontlines arrives on February 4.

[h3]Free Operation Pass[/h3]

For those enjoying the free Operation Passes each month, that experience will remain largely unchanged.

Playing [i]Halo Infinite[/i] during the active window of the Operation lets you unlock 20 reward tiers as you complete matches and earn XP. However, if you’re unable to finish all or part of it during the month, the free customization content will be available to acquire with Spartan Points (earned simply by completing matches) via The Exchange as part of [i]Infinite[/i]’s next major update (the Summer Update in this specific case).

Play during the month when an Operation is live and mop up all the customization items in the free Pass, or seek them out at your leisure when they hit The Exchange later down the line.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/de31fbdacd08c26e86af8a87195ccec08ce77c58.jpg[/img]

[h3]Premium Operation Pass[/h3]

The Premium Operation Pass is receiving an extensive overhaul, including an increase in size, bringing greater value for players who decide to upgrade.

[b]This expanded pass will be available in the first Operation of each Update. The second and third Operations will offer the traditional 20-tier Operation Pass offering.[/b]

The Premium Pass supports the usual perks: It makes the Operation Pass durable (it will not expire), offers bonus XP during the Operation’s live window, and provides an extra Challenge slot while your Pass is equipped.

But where previous Operation Passes have featured one armor set—one particular “look” for your Spartan—the new incarnation of this Premium Pass will now offer four full armor sets. These will be unlocked as you progress through 50 tiers of rewards.

The price of the Premium Operation Pass has been slightly adjusted for this offering, providing the following options:
[list][*] 1,000 Credits: The Operation Pass is durable, offers bonus XP, provides an extra Challenge slot, and immediately gives you multiple bonus items. Provides the ability to earn four full armor sets.
[*] 2,500 Credits: All of the above, and instantly unlocks the first 20 levels out of 50.[/list]
Players must purchase Premium Passes during the time the Operation is live, as it will not be available for purchase once that month-long window has closed. If you miss out on purchasing any Premium Operation Pass going forward but want the armor it offered, you will be able to find it in the Shop during the next seasonal update (and at an adjusted price).

But the best value really does come with the Operation Pass. For just 1,000 Credits, you will gain the ability to earn FOUR full armor sets—one free, three premium. As noted, the free armor will flow into The Exchange, while the other three armor sets will later return in the Shop. So you’ll definitely want to make sure you grab all four armor sets while the Premium Pass is available as you will secure them early for a [i]steep[/i] discount before they enter the Shop.

Obviously, these are some significant changes to the format, and we are eager to continue listening to feedback from players as you get your hands on Operation: Frontlines and this updated experience. Let us know what you think!

Secure the Premium Pass for access to all 50 tiers and instantly unlock the BR75A2 Hammer weapon model for the BR75 Battle Rifle, Xenothreat weapon coating, Sequence Assembly weapon charm, and Pattern Seeker visor.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Mode: Assault[/h2]

The Assault mode—a fan-favorite since [i]Halo 2[/i]—is en route to [i]Halo Infinite[/i]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/9c1e52b591b834b925d063d46439cd39e35d72f2.jpg[/img]

Each team defends their bomb site as they battle over a neutral bomb in the center of the map, aiming to escort the intrepid and heroic bomb carrier to the enemy base to arm and detonate it.

Of course, Assault is a mode that comes with multiple variants as well. When it arrives with the Spring Update, you’ll be able to play both Neutral Bomb and One Bomb.

The bombastic action will be available in both 4v4 and Squad Battle’s 8v8 modes. So, if you’ve been jonesing for some One Bomb on High Ground or Kusini Bay, the wait ends soon.

For more information, be sure to check out the Assault Playlist Blog when it launches next Tuesday.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Sandbox Updates[/h2]
[h3][u]Weapons[/u][/h3]

[b]Heatwave[/b]

Previously, the vertical fire on the Heatwave was set in a custom position providing a consistent close to long range damage output making this a deadly shotgun-like weapon from all ranges. To address player feedback about the Heatwave being too effective at longer ranges, we’ve made changes to how its projectiles behave while using its vertical shot.

In addition to a slightly slower rate of fire for the weapon all-up, the vertical fire projectiles will now slowly spread out as they travel further distances. This spread now matches the characteristics of the horizontal fire, helping to reduce its performance at range.
[list][*] Distribution Function: Custom Position >> Custom Direction
[*] Rounds per second: 1.54 >> 1.34[/list]
[b]Stalker Rifle[/b]

The Stalker Rifle has been emerging as an extremely powerful weapon in Arena gameplay, especially after the Bandit’s rate-of-fire was decreased. To keep the Stalker Rifle’s power in check relative to the Bandit, it will also be getting a rate-of-fire decrease.

The Stalker Rifle should still be an important on-map pickup, but it shouldn’t feel like a one-sided fight when going up against it anymore.
[list][*] Rounds per second: 2.3 >> 2.2[/list]
[b]Disruptor[/b]

The Disruptor, which is part of the Pistol class of weapons, has been overperforming outside of its intended range, much like previous iterations of the Mk50 Sidekick. The damage output at close range feels like it’s in a good place, but its ability to deal that damage at mid-to-long range—specifically against enemy Spartans at those distances—was proving to be too much.

To minimize the effectiveness at long ranges against Spartans, the bloom properties are getting an update. It’s also important to note that while we wanted to reduce its impact on Spartans at range, it’s critical that the weapon retains its ability to EMP vehicles over long distances in larger battlefields.

When the update launches, the Disruptor will take longer to have its bloom reset and have increased error angles, resulting in less impact on smaller targets at range.

On Ranked maps, the Disruptor will also have its initial ammo reduced to ensure its total kill potential can remain in check.
[list][*] Min error angle[list][*] (Low) 0.125 >> 0.2
[*] (High) 0.125 >> 0.35[/list][*] Max error angle[list][*] (Low) 0.35 >> 0.35
[*] (High) 0.8 >> 1[/list][*] Lower bound deceleration time: 0 >> 0.56
[*] Upper bound deceleration time: 0.365 >> 0.43
[*] Reduced starting ammo amount on Ranked maps: 12 | 36 >> 12 | 12[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/5e2945e39ae0e8a33405b2915c7437ff16c27428.jpg[/img]

[b]CQ248 Bulldog[/b]

Similar to the Stalker Rifle, the Bulldog also had started to emerge as an extremely impactful weapon after the Bandit’s rate-of-fire reduction. To ensure players have a more balanced fight when going up against the Bulldog, its rate-of-fire will be slowing down slightly, and its headshot multiplier will be removed. These adjustments should help the Bulldog’s power better align with the rest of the sandbox.
[list][*] Rounds per second: 1.67 >> 1.55
[*] Headshot damage multiplier on health: 2 >> 0[/list]
[b]Shock Rifle[/b]

The Shock Rifle has demonstrated greater effectiveness at longer ranges than anticipated when used in hip fire. To encourage zooming in for long-range engagements, the range at which aim magnetism kicks in will be brought in a bit. Since no-scoping was also proving to be a little too easy at high-skill levels, the auto-aim angles have been adjusted to make each shot more skillful when firing from the hip.
[list][*] Reduced autoaim angle: 0.5 >> 0.2
[*] Reduced magnetism angle: 3 >> 2
[*] Reduced magnetism range: 25 >> 20
[*] Reduced magnetism falloff range: 14 >> 12[/list]
[b]MA40 AR[/b]

In a previous update, the MA40 AR received a tuning pass that adjusted its bloom properties. While it increased the consistency of the weapon at full bloom, we heard the feedback that it bloomed out too quickly, with many stating that they missed its accuracy on the first few shots. In response to that feedback, we’ll be bringing those initial shots back to their previous state.

To help balance out the feel of this initial buff, the AR’s max bloom state when going fully-auto will be expanded more and its headshot multiplier will be removed.
[list][*] Initial accuracy improved
[list][*] Lower bound deceleration time: 0.3 >> 0.22
[*] Deceleration time: 0.24 >> 0.17[/list] [*] Maximum error angle
[list][*] (Low): 0.25 >> 0.25
[*] (High): 1.3 >> 2.1[/list][*] Headshot damage multiplier on health: 2.55 >> 0
[*] Reduced starting ammo amount on Ranked maps: 36 | 108 >> 36 | 36[/list]

[h3][u]Grenades[/u][/h3]

[b]Frag Grenade Physics[/b]

Frag Grenade Physics

The “bounciness” of Frag Grenades has been increased, allowing players to make creative, skillful plays. This will bring the bounce physics a little more in line with previous titles, while also reducing instances of grenades feeling stuck to the ground or not having successful bounces.
[list][*] Perpendicular friction (between 90-80 degrees): 0.825 >> 0.78
[*] Perpendicular friction (between 50-80 degrees): 0.8 >> 0.78
[*] Perpendicular friction (between 20-50 degrees): 0.75 >> 0.72[/list]
[b]Grenade Cast Time[/b]

[i]Halo Infinite[/i]’s grenade cast time—aka the time it takes for a player to throw a grenade and reset—was the fastest in the franchise by a pretty large margin.

For example, here are some average rates (grenades per second) from previous games:
[list][*] [i]Halo: CE[/i]: 1.07
[*] [i]Halo 2[/i]: 1.13
[*] [i]Halo 3[/i]: 1.07
[*] [i]Halo: Reach[/i]: 0.99
[*] [i]Halo 4[/i]: 0.89
[*] [i]Halo Infinite[/i] (before): 0.79[/list]
While grenades are a key element of [i]Halo[/i] gameplay, we felt that the ability to throw multiple grenades at such a rapid rate or throw a grenade and then shoot quickly after was having a negative effect on the core combat loop.

To help improve the feel of the [i]Halo[/i] combat dance, we’ll be bringing the grenade throw rate more in line with previous titles. This should both reduce the feeling of “grenade spam” and increase the intentionality of each grenade thrown.
[list][*] [i]Halo Infinite[/i] (updated): 0.92[/list]
[h3][u]Movement[/u][/h3]

[b]Strafe Acceleration[/b]

It’s happening!

Strafe acceleration values are being updated to improve the feel of gameplay engagements across the board. This adjustment will help address community feedback on topics such as jiggle-peeking behind cover and reduce instances of opponents changing directions at seemingly unnatural speeds when strafing.

The adjustment to these strafe scalars should bring the overall “feel” of [i]Halo Infinite[/i]’s combat even more in line with previous [i]Halo[/i] titles.
[list][*] Acceleration strafe scalar: 1 >> 0.78
[*] Acceleration forward scalar: 1 >> 0.78[/list]
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Ranked Updates[/h2]
[h3]New Ranked Map & Ranked Map Refresh[/h3]

A new map has arrived in Ranked!

[b]Origin[/b]
Credits: Karmaplex, DarkMaiming, HiImMike

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/a00da152f968f86d4437534751d9c7f8aed731b5.jpg[/img]

A fan-favorite returns as Origin, a remake of Coliseum from [i]Halo 5: Guardians[/i] makes its way into [i]Halo Infinite[/i]’s Ranked playlists. Remade in Forge, you’ll get to see the map with [i]Halo Infinite[/i]’s Forerunner aesthetics.

Origin will be playable in Ranked Arena, Ranked Slayer, and Ranked Doubles when Operation: Frontlines drops. It will also appear in regular matchmaking playlists as well.

[h3]New Mode[/h3]

We’re excited to add a new mode to Ranked: Assault! The legacy game mode is just how you remember it—plant the bomb in the enemy team’s base to score a point. Ranked Arena will feature Assault:Neutral Bomb Ranked on both Aquarius and Fortress. The score to win is 3 points.

[h3]New Ranked Rotational Playlist – Ranked Squad Battle[/h3]

Feeling in the mood for some competitive action but with a larger number of players, more spacious maps, and wider sandbox variety? Ranked Squad Battle will be your next destination!

Get the squad ready, it’s gonna get sweaty—8v8, Bandit Evo starts, and a variety of modes to compete on, including our new mode Assault.

Assault will be available in Ranked Squad Battle in two forms: Neutral Bomb and One Bomb! Assault: One Bomb Ranked makes its debut on two iconic maps: Kusini Bay and Refuge, remakes of [i]Halo 2[/i]’s Zanzibar and Headlong respectively.

[h3]Ranked Map Updates[/h3]

With a new Ranked season incoming, it’s time again for a sandbox refresh to our Ranked maps. Below, you will find the changes we’ve made to sandbox items and their locations on Ranked Arena maps.

[b]Aquarius[/b]
[list][*] Camo replacing Overshield top middle
[*] Threat seeker replaced the plasma grenades on Hydro[/list]
[b]Emyprean[/b]
[list][*] Assault Rifle and Commando Rifle swap locations
[*] Plasma Pistol moved to Alley
[*] Repulsor moved to Terminal
[*] Overshield moved to Underpass[/list]
[b]Forbidden[/b]
[list][*] Battle Rifles to the front of Bases
[*] Thrust replaced the Threat seeker at Big Door[/list]
[b]Live Fire[/b]
[list][*] Battle Rifle added to Turbine[/list]
[b]Recharge[/b]
[list][*] Shock Rifle has been placed on a power weapon pad to align with the properties of Solitude[/list]
[b]Solitude[/b]
[list][*] Commando Rifle replaced Bandit at Bottom Mid
[*] Added Battle Rifle to Blue Ramp[/list]
[b]Streets[/b]
[list][*] Bulldog replaced with a Sidekick at Commercial District[/list]
Additionally, to keep the experience fresh and address points of feedback we’ve received from Ranked players, we are adding some new geometry to a few of the maps. Specifically, we’ve added new jumps to some of our core maps in Ranked to improve map flow and create new routes for players. These new jump routes will only be available on the “Ranked” versions of Aquarius, Forbidden, Recharge, and Streets. Stay tuned for more details on these.

[h3]Matchmaking Rank Reset[/h3]

It’s that time again. All Ranked playlists will have ranks resetting with the release of Operation: Frontlines!

New playlists, new map, new modes, new sandbox balances, map pool changes and more. There are a [i]lot[/i] of changes coming to Ranked and there is no better time to start fresh and jump in. We’ll see you out there. Good luck, Spartans!
[hr][/hr]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/4aadd0e8b0017783553394be67207dca5c698535.jpg[/img]

[h2]Forge Updates[/h2]

The Fuel Rod SPNKr and Bomb object have been added to Forge as objects which should allow for some explosive opportunities to create new experiences.

In addition to these new sandbox objects, Forge will also be getting some improvements to better support mode creation. These additions should unlock more power—and add more polish—to modes across the board, all while helping to bridge the gap between Forge and our internal tools.
[list][*] Increased Nav Marker functionality for fine-tuned control, including when a player takes damage, is sprinting, or is in another player’s line of sight
[*] Added the ability to Set Object Team for multiple generic objectives, with more on the way
[*] Improved control of Generic Objective objects when entering Kill Volumes
[*] Enhanced physics controls for objects through Set Object Physics Mode (Normal, Zero Gravity, and Fixed)
[*] Inclusion of Damage Source Object input pin allows for better kill attribution by selecting a player to be the source on the Apply Damage node[/list]
For a more detailed look at these Forge additions, be sure to read the Patch Notes on February 4!

[hr][/hr]
That’s a wrap on our overview for the 2025 Spring Update in [i]Halo Infinite[/i].

We’re incredibly excited for you to get hands-on with all the new offerings, so keep sending your feedback our way. We’ll catch you on February 4 when Operation: Frontlines arrives!

notes.title: Action Sack
notes.content:
No preamble, you’ve waited long enough…Welcome to Action Sack, where weird ‘n’ wild warfare brings mayhem and madness in a myriad of modes! 

[previewyoutube=9JfHeLHiNeA;full][/previewyoutube]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Rules of Engagement[/h2]

Action Sack is the playlist where the rules are a little less clear per mode because it’s not as straightforward as “First to 50 wins.” This playlist is made up of several different Free-For-All minigames that will leave you laughing. Baptism by fire is the best way to learn!

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Maps & Modes[/h2]

Without any further ado, let’s check out what fun we’ll be having!

[h3]Duck Hunt[/h3]
Credits: MikRips
Bookmarks: [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/2763df6b-51b9-4af7-87fd-a27aa3fed34d]Map[/url] | [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/modes/3cb0806d-a85e-43a7-a37e-60b2b5ab0383]Mode[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/3110d6c0af5116d5e28b3186874bb35d0a714f54.jpg[/img]

The goal is to get from point A to point B without losing your hat to the sniper in the middle of the ring. Dodge, duck, dip, dive, and dodge your way to the end!

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Goose Hunt[/h3]
Credits: ArturBloodshot
Bookmarks: [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/53aa6c36-22c3-47a1-ade0-76ec3232ec46]Map[/url] | [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/modes/14ce711b-2bb9-4673-a2cb-c16b2bbb64d4]Mode[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/93e2041c5af6d7fc6504aa9ef75923ce4e5abf4e.jpg[/img]

This deceptively easy mode has you driving a Mongoose along a narrow path that curves around in a large circle. The catch? You’re going to be dodging SPNKr rounds from the player that is “it” so don’t fall off the edge. Get on your Mongoose and ride!

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Hex-A-Gone[/h3]
Credits: unsorted guy
Bookmarks: [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/1dd15994-5197-4985-bedd-fe1824e56a2d]Map[/url] | [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/modes/a68791bf-45d7-4d68-915f-adcca94d8952]Mode[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/571ba7c77c9ddb17900a27d71d051a07d9b2fadb.jpg[/img]

If you’ve played a certain popular free-for-all game where the goal is to avoid falling over, then you’ve likely played Hex-A-Gone before. As you walk across each tile, it’ll fall so hop from tile to tile, avoid falling to the next level as long as you can. Think “the floor is lava” style.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Maze Craze[/h3]
Bookmarks: [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/modes/07d63a23-56ab-4ba5-9587-195b0f20c12b]Map[/url] | [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/modes/07d63a23-56ab-4ba5-9587-195b0f20c12b]Mode[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/0a0b3dc308968372d8658191f89d2592f818c762.jpg[/img]

It’s a maze so you’re bound to get turned around and lost but that’s okay. There is no prize or goal at the center…you’re just avoiding the Spartan with the Gravity Hammer and trying to be the last one standing.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Speedball[/h3]
Bookmarks: [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/58be6588-b596-437d-94a6-7821741c311e]Map[/url] | [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/modes/dde764a3-f915-4405-839c-67caef6b1de8]Mode[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/00ed75b9203032d311bf46ea040f097b6bb887c1.jpg[/img]

On your marks…get set…go! Rush the Oddball in the middle of the field while evading all the rockets and hammers around you. Hold the ball to score points…but speedily. Gotta go fast!

[hr][/hr]
It’s crazy chaos and fantastic fun for all. Grab your friends and jump into Action Sack today!

[i]Quack for me.[/i]

notes.title: Castle Wars
notes.content:
When it was introduced to matchmaking in [i]Halo 5[/i], Castle Wars quickly became a fan favorite. The large-scale assault on the enemy’s base to grab the flag led to high-risk, high reward plays that kept us all coming back for more.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/d338591d7ad84afa501ce77c956b262aaef47436.jpg[/img]

And that’s why we’re excited to see Castle Wars added to [i]Halo Infinite[/i]!

[hr][/hr]
[h2]The Base-ics[/h2]

It’s an amped up version of 8v8 Capture the Flag that necessitates your team breaking through the defenses of the opponent’s heavily fortified castles.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/5cdb81c541b9b661870ca5de6f6b9d5e18b0de71.jpg[/img]

Grab their flag and make your way back to your base to score while dodging the oncoming horde of enemy Spartans.

Everyone is equipped with an Energy Sword and a Grappleshot. As a bonus, you can use your Grapple while holding the Flag, so beware the sneaky fly-bys.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]My Kingdom for a Castle[/h2]

You can’t have Castle Wars without the castles, so let’s check out the fortresses you’ll be assaulting! Also, huge thank you to erickyboo for creating the mode and one or two of the maps.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Gothic[/h3]
Credits: erickyboo
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/5667a22a-2bb2-42de-902f-5553b0a2cc68]Bookmark[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/7a5f1ea11ea8fe3a7d9b556659e6a7070e46d2d2.jpg[/img]

Pointed arches? Check. Verticality? Check. Flying buttresses? Check. Definitely Gothic in nature.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Harvesters[/h3]
Credits: erickyboo
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/695b8417-cb74-4ed8-9d62-12470cf734b5]Bookmark[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/13e05cd91725e1fb4dd3ea984fa3d564840a1cbf.jpg[/img]

As long as it doesn’t take you five long years to steal the enemy flag…

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Gondolas[/h2]
Credits: erickyboo
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/695b8417-cb74-4ed8-9d62-12470cf734b5]Bookmark[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/4d67d4e84ec75da2223b4b4ce5a71fe949938d0b.jpg[/img]

Just you, your weapon, and fifteen others out for a leisurely jaunt on the gondolas.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Yosai[/h3]
Credits: erickyboo
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/0fffef26-d737-4482-8c8f-7a592bfb81ab]Bookmark[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/8491e4e229ad01b2392e2379fe1fae2c261ffdb3.jpg[/img]

Find your inner Zen before the chaos of battle ensues.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Sunken[/h3]
Credits: erickyboo, BizzyBum, goobot
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/06cfd6c7-4682-4586-97f0-d83cd6c7bc43]Bookmark[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/a64be75b34abbdcc1d61e8ba5300016180d837a4.jpg[/img]

Whatever you do, remember that Spartans can’t swim, so don’t jump off the edge.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Promenade[/h3]
Credits: erickyboo
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/960732c6-642e-4065-8f3f-13c140131b7f]Bookmark[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/52df596bd3011c6c89e4e160de76767d3a911f8e.jpg[/img]

You’ll be dancing in and out of the beams of the neon moon down the Promenade.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Nadair[/h3]
Credits: DISTORTED JAKAL, LudoHT
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/688c6c16-0afe-41dc-ad47-97492ce50887]Bookmark[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/6dfabf031c81783c7ffabc26b84afd2c29613ead.jpg[/img]

This fortress is everything you’d expect a medieval castle to be.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Jarok Bridge[/h3]
Credits: Halo Studios
[url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/5763f971-ec5f-4b05-a9f3-aee8f625163f]Bookmark[/url]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/05af67cedecd83aef12771d4a275585b64c4a15d.jpg[/img]

Some bridges are meant to be burnt.

[hr][/hr]

That’s that! So remember, charge ahead, battle through the defenders, make your way through the castle, grab the Flag, and get back to your base to score.

[i]Bye bye, Spartans, have fun storming the castles![/i]

notes.title: Snowball Fight
notes.content:
Winter has come to Halo Infinite, and with it, a flurry of excitement with the introduction of a veritable Snowball Fight.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/23f4e763fcce45b89659243348fd9d63c7d5065b.jpg[/img]

That’s right. It’s time to be merry! ❄️

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Unleashing the Snowballs[/h2]

Forget about the conventional arsenal of weapons; in Snowball Fight, the battlefield is ruled by the infinite supply of plasma grenades. Dip, dodge, and duck other team’s plasmas while launching your own. This is a team-based race to 50 so be sure to watch your teammate’s back too! As a bonus, you’ll be doing all this in Third-Person so you get the additional thrill of watching “snowballs” whiz by you as you enter the fray.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]A Winter Wonderland[/h2]

It wouldn’t be a snowball fight without snow and we’ve got three winter wonderlands for you to romp around on.

[h3]Snow Fire[/h3]
Credits: Halo Studios

notes.title: 1v1 Showdown
notes.content:
Guess what’s back. Back again—tell a friend. Today, the 1v1 Showdown makes its official debut in matchmaking!

[hr][/hr]
[h2]1v1 Me Bro. For Real This Time.[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/c5890f67e3c926659f90f52ae862f7ff721348d3.jpg[/img]

One of the most common pieces of feedback we heard during the Combat Workshop outing was that you would love to take a friend with you for the ultimate showdown. We heard you loud and clear and the playlist has been updated to allow parties of two to search.

Thanks to Forger Artifice, you can now [i]literally[/i] challenge someone to a 1v1 and duke it out on the battlefield for the ultimate bragging rights.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Rules of Engagement[/h2]

Before you jump in, you should know what you’re getting into and how to win. The victor is the first to win the best of 5 rounds. If you’re asking “How do I win a round?” we have you covered. You can win in one of two ways:
[list][*] Be the first to 5 kills
[*] Capture the zone[/list]
Each round is a race to 5 with spawns resetting immediately after a kill happens to ensure everyone is on an even playing field. However, if at any point during the round someone captures a hill, they win the round. Yes, this means you can be down 4-1, capture the zone, and still win the round.

Both players will be equipped identically with random loadouts that vary from round to round. You never know what you’ll have in your pockets so be nimble and ready to flex your strategy to adapt to the gear you might find.

Just to keep you on your toes, you may be granted a round modifier (you’ll see the UI banner pop up) that adds a new twist to the game. Keep your reflexes sharp and be ready to adjust to whatever the game throws you, including a damage boost, low gravity, or amped up speed. You never know whatcha gonna get.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Lay of the Land[/h2]

So, you’ve thrown the gauntlet and are ready to face off in the 1v1, meaning you’ve got the who and the what. Now all you need is where. We have found that standard Arena maps are slightly too large for 1v1, so with the help of community Forger UneeQ, we’ve taken slices of some of your favorite maps and created a unique set of battlefields.

Between rounds, loadouts aren’t the only thing that changes—you’ll be teleported to a new map slice so the scenery will also stay fresh. Here are the maps that have had slices pulled from them:

[h3]Aquarius[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/69f8dcf522908998543b6650f3c9addae98ee7a4.jpg[/img]

[h3]Argyle[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/05af8762e8501124ac011452f4c459d321fb9947.jpg[/img]

[h3]Bazaar[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/e399cbaec528e3537f8a93b33714b6f486c1dea5.jpg[/img]

[h3]Catalyst[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/fd70174c8dac1eca5784bf4e51949b1d305e26ce.jpg[/img]

[h3]Empyrean[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/b4b90a13afac3d8580da8de0aae16fc04400a0d2.jpg[/img]

[h3]Fortress*[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/e746af9cb26f81f65f6bf835d8820f852df29f12.jpg[/img]

[h3]Origin*[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/1ea6dfeba367916808d4fea0787112a03166b23d.jpg[/img]

[i]*Fortress and Origin slices are making their debut with the full release of the playlist, with Origin joining the full map pool at a later date.[/i]

[hr][/hr]

If you can talk the talk, you better be able to walk the walk so challenge your friend and put your skills to the test!

notes.title: Combat Workshop: 1v1 Showdown
notes.content:
Previously seen at HCS Salt Lake City and the 2024 Halo World Championship, the 1v1 Showdown experience is making its way to Combat Workshop for everyone to enjoy!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/411ed01ba0de1804e6de4dccabd2a19692072fe5.jpg[/img]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]1v1 Me, Bro[/h2]

If you pride yourself on your ability to take on other Spartans head-to-head, then you’ll love the 1v1 Showdown. If the first round didn’t go your way, just take a deep breath and try again. The best of 5 wins and each round can be won in one of two ways:
[list][*] Getting 5 kills
[*] Capturing the zone[/list]
[previewyoutube=66WTGTaimjw;full][/previewyoutube]

Remember to keep a sharp eye on the capture timer because a smart opponent will take advantage of that and will sneak a capture right under your nose for the point. Both players will be equipped with identical loadouts that are randomized. Primaries, secondaries, grenades, and equipment will change from round to round. Additionally, you may occasionally receive a round modifier that will be denoted via UI banner. This could be anything from a Damage Boost, to low gravity—so keep your eyes peeled and your reflexes sharp.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Name the Place[/h2]

If you feel a sense of déjà vu while playing, that is entirely understandable since the maps are small slices of well known and loved maps. Each round sees you teleported to a new map slice to keep things fresh. Here are the maps that the combat spaces have been pulled from:
[list][*] Aquarius
[*] Argyle
[*] Bazaar
[*] Catalyst
[*] Empyrean[/list]
[hr][/hr]
[b]Have thoughts? Be sure to follow up and provide your feedback![/b]

The Combat Workshop is your one-shop stop to check out work-in-progress maps, modes, and other new experiences. This playlist allows us to test out new modes, new features, new experiences, and get feedback at-scale before taking that information back and iterating on it. From there, we can address issues and community feedback to get things ready for primetime matchmaking.

The survey will go live [b]Thursday, November 14,[/b] so check back for the link then.

[hr][/hr]

The 1v1 Showdown Combat Workshop will be live until November 19 so jump in, take on your opponents, and give us your feedback when the survey is available!
