tags.balance_change: As announced and released on February 28, we’ve made an update to the ranking system to match based on CSR as opposed to MMR.
The Fireteam CSR Limit range has not changed as part of this update and is as follows:
For 899 CSR (Gold 6) or lower, there are no restrictions.
At 900 CSR (Platinum 1) a limit of 900 points is introduced.
Between 900 CSR (Platinum 1) and 1500 CSR (Onyx) the Fireteam CSR limit will slowly tighten as you climb the ranks.
It will start at the 900 limit mentioned above and tighten to its final destination of 500.
This essentially means that on the way to Onyx, every 2 CSR gained will tighten the Fireteam limit by an increment of 1 CSR
At 1500 CSR and above, the limit is 600 points
In order to alleviate this, we’re reducing the placement matches required from 10 to 5.

notes.title: Maps & Mode Preview | Season 3
notes.content:
Season 3 of [i]Halo Infinite[/i] arrives on March 7.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/d1fedc0505429c9c10afc02b4c826341d7106f1f.png[/img]

A new season means new maps! Season 3: Echoes Within brings with it a trio of exciting and unique spaces for your regularly scheduled online Spartan-slaying. These maps are Oasis, Cliffhanger, and Chasm.

We’re joined today by a terrific trio of our veritable multiplayer designers – Cliff Schuldt (Multiplayer Level Designer), Donnie Taylor (Art Director), and Kim Haines (Lead MP Env. Technical Artist) – for a Q&A deep-dive into these new maps, the process of creating them, the fun we’ve had on them, and more…

Of course, before we get into talking about these maps, how about we show them off in their full majesty with a new flythrough video?

[previewyoutube=Ho8m9Q9Wz5U;full][/previewyoutube]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Maps[/h2]
[i][b]I’m super excited to be able to talk with you about the three new maps coming in Season 3! To start off, let’s give each of them a general introduction – how would you summarize these maps so Halo fans have a sense of what they’re in for with these spaces?[/b][/i]

CS: Oasis is a mosh pit of pure vehicular fun for BTB, and it’s got a stunning skybox with a Forerunner ship terraforming the desert environment around it.

Cliffhanger is set at an ONI black site atop a mountain, also featuring man cannons for maximum vertigo!

Chasm is what you’d get if you took Boarding Action from [i]Halo: CE[/I] and put in some Grappleshots, which is every bit as fun as it sounds.

[i][b]To dive into Oasis, the first thing I think we have to do is marvel at that stunning vista – that’s as much a staple of Halo as the complexities of its design, to my mind. Can you tell us a bit about what goes into creating a skybox on a Halo map?[/b][/i]

DT: When production starts for our skybox, or really any art asset, we begin with concepting several mood sketches that depict time of day and any major feature that we want to put on display for the vista. In the case of Oasis, that was the large Forerunner structure.

We use those concepts to help guide us to a final direction and that becomes the visual target for the game art moving forward. This direction is not fully set in stone as translating ideas from 2D to 3D always has its curveballs, but the overall goal is to stay true in game to the hook that first drew us to select the original 2D piece.

[i][b]I definitely get some Halo 4 BTB map vibes from Oasis. Were there any specific inspirations that were part of the development of this map?[/b][/i]

CS: There are elements of inspiration taken from the map Exile from [i]Halo 4[/i], which was a BTB favorite back in the day, with the emphasis on more open space for lots of fun vehicular action.

CTF modes were particularly exciting on this map during testing, as vehicles allow for some truly epic flag capture runs. Practically every space here is accessible with a Warthog, even the interior spaces. So you can go out into the open, where you might be more at risk of falling prey to air or heavy vehicles, or you can drive through some of the interior spaces where those other vehicles are going to have a much harder time catching you and risk getting boxed in.

That risk/reward aspect of [i]Halo[/i]’s vehicular gameplay is always incredibly engaging, and we think Oasis is a great showcase of that.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/02e603d85650658d04f2b8d2fee23e47cf4a659a.jpg[/img]

[I][b]Let’s shift over to Cliffhanger – so aptly named because this ONI facility is set on the edge of a cliff. What are some of the unique elements of this map?[/b][/i]

DT: Biome diversity is always a big one for us when it comes to multiplayer maps. We want these spaces to feel different from past maps we’ve offered – and even where we might be using a similar “theme,” like a human base, we have unique visual elements to tap into.

An ONI black site is going to look quite different to the more traditional UNSC aesthetic of Live Fire, or the water treatment facility of Recharge. And there’s a subtle Forerunner element in this map you might pick up on as well.

[i][b]What are some of the design considerations that go into creating an asymmetrical Arena map like this?[/b][/i]

CS: Cliffhanger was originally designed with zone control modes (like Strongholds and King of the Hill) in mind, and what that means is that each “zone” has to look and feel unique.

There’s a bit of a “rock, paper, scissors” dynamic that zone control modes have in terms of how you tactically consider what your team is going to go for – if we go for Zone A and C, we might lose out on B, but that location might end up being a solid base for the enemy team to make a comeback if we’ve divided our forces across the map, and so on.

That goes on to inform sightlines, weapons spawns, equipment placement… everything ties back into how you can work together with your team to control areas of the map.

[i][b]Something I always enjoy about asymmetric maps are the “scenarios” that are naturally created by the map layout – like on Halo 3’s High Ground where the turret above the door to the enemy base creates the sense of a “siege.” What are some of those focal points on Cliffhanger?[/b][/i]

CS: What we really felt as we were testing this map was how different it feels depending on which mode you’re playing. One Flag, for example, creates a more “linear asymmetric” experience in a similar vein to the example you gave of High Ground – attackers and defenders are not just put on different ends of the map, it feels like they’re in different “scenarios.”

Of course, when you then play a mode like Strongholds, you get a totally different experience of the map. We hope that creates a cool dynamic that players enjoy.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/147e2ca3395db7b4a50766f72db441276e0e44fa.jpg[/img]

[i][b]We’ve got a third map coming as well when Season 3 drops. Chasm looks and feels quite different to the other maps in Halo Infinite, so how did this map come to be?[/b][/i]

CS: This map came to be when my friend Andrew and I were running through the [i]Halo Infinite[/i] Campaign Network Co-Op flight. As we were playing through the second mission, Foundation, we were goofing off in a particular area and I thought this could be a fun space to play in for multiplayer.

So, I investigated this, pulling the space into a multiplayer level (note: this was definitely a more involved process than ctrl-C and ctrl-V!) and redoing the layout to be a rotational symmetrical map to support CTF.

After the first couple of playtests, the map was received really well, and we decided to give it the full treatment to pull it in as an official map.

Even though it looks incredibly similar to a space in the campaign, it has been laid out – and thus plays – very differently. One of the things I think is awesome about this map is the risk of falling into the “chasm” (har har!), but with the Grappleshot you can actually turn that to your advantage and make some incredibly cool skill jumps and maneuvers that turns falling from a danger of death to a risk/reward “route” through the map.

[i][b]While the other two maps have Forerunner elements in them, Chasm is entirely Forerunner-themed. What are some of the unique visual and gameplay factors of this particular palette that offer something fresh?[/b][/i]

CS: I think the visuals of this space are awesome. Being in the cavernous depths of Zeta Halo has this eerie and mysterious feeling in the campaign, and that really translates to the map as well – the Art Team knocked it out of the park!

Something we did to help visually differentiate parts of the map is that one side has that traditional cool blue tone you often see in Forerunner spaces, while the other side has a greater emphasis on the gold element you see in places like the Silent Auditorium in the campaign.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/2d9056f11c693dd1409a4feb136fe153b38ea63b.jpg[/img]

[i][b]How do you think the new sandbox additions – namely, the M392 Bandit and Shroud Screen – will change up the way these maps are played?[/b][/i]

CS: Oh, I think they’re both strong additions! A lot of the feedback we got from players on Chasm noted that it felt like the Bandit worked really well for the kind of ranges you have on that map.

Shroud has been great on Oasis as well. It’s fun to “smoke” a long sightline before pulling a flag – we’ve seen some amazing “Houdini” plays around it!

[i][b]We’ve previously stated that we’re bringing editable dev maps to Forge in Season 3. Does that include these three maps as well?[/b][/i]

KH: Yes! Each of these maps are editable on release, along with all the previously shipped Arena and BTB maps. Future maps will be editable on release as well.

[i][b]What modes can players expect to be playing on these maps? Do you have any you’re especially excited about players getting to experience?[/b][/i]

CS: Well, I am a sucker for CTF, so I have really enjoyed CTF matches on these maps quite a bit. On Oasis, there have been some truly incredible flag runs with Warthogs and Banshees chasing you down through the caves.

On Cliffhanger, Strongholds, KOTH, and One-Flag have been super fun. There are a lot of great opportunities to push people into death pits with the Repulsor, and using a man cannon to fly across the map into the hill location has been a fun (and risky) way to assault the other team.

I will say that people should load up KOTH on Chasm to see one of the [i]spiciest[/i] hill locations [i]Halo[/i] has ever seen.

And then, of course, there’s the new Escalation Slayer mode coming in Season 3 as well. We can’t wait for everyone to jump into that!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/dd3451464a1fba47507826e95e94c10670457b83.jpg[/img]

[i][b]Do you have any fun stories from playtests on these maps?[/b][/i]

CS: Oh, absolutely!

On Oasis, I was driving a Warthog with Brian Berryhill on the turret during a CTF match and we managed to do all three flag captures. We had a Wasp on our tail throughout, which we managed to shake off in a tunnel, only to emerge and find an enemy Scorpion on the other side – but we managed to escape that as well and steal the flag. By the time we got back to base, we had wheels missing, our Warthog was on fire, but we won and the tension around whether we would make it was absolutely exhilarating!

On Cliffhanger, there’s a man cannon that sends you over a death pit, and using the Repulsor to knock enemies who are chasing you off the map is tremendous fun. There’s an elevator shaft elsewhere on the map, as well as some sneaky mountainside paths, and the Repulsor and Grappleshot really bring a new dynamic to the danger of those kinds of locations.

Finally, Chasm. People loved faking their deaths on this map – pretending to jump off the edge into the abyss, only to use the Grappleshot to swing back up with incredible momentum that can have them sailing through the air to another part of the map.

There was one situation where a player got to the Active Camo spawn a little early, putting him in danger of getting picked off from an exposed position, and so he jumped off the hex pillar to use it as cover and zipped back around to grab the Camo as it spawned in. It was this dawning realization that we’ve never been able to play [i]Halo[/i] quite like this before, and we really are excited to see some of the insane plays people are going to have.

[i][b]Thank you very much for taking the time to chat about the maps coming in Season 3! Do you have any parting words before we wrap this up?[/b][/i]

We’ve put some fun little Easter eggs on these maps (some sandwich-related, others we’re going to let you find yourselves), so do let us know if you find anything interesting…

And, as mentioned above, we really can’t wait to see what kinds of plays you make on these maps – whether that’s a heroic flag capture on Oasis, mountainside tumbles courtesy of the Repulsor on Cliffhanger, or Grappleshot fake-outs on Chasm. Absolutely tag us with your clips and montages, we’d love to see them!

Huge shoutout to our partners who helped bring these maps together, and to our players as well who we hope are really going to enjoy what we’ve been cooking up for Season 3.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Escalation Slayer[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/c95b3a50352163230f3947a3c6497e5bf4d6221b.jpg[/img]

Also coming in Season 3 is the Escalation Slayer game mode.

Escalation Slayer is a mode that some of you may have played in [i]Halo: MCC,[/i] as it came to the collection in the Series 6: Raven update back in April 2021 and quickly became a fan favorite – and now it is coming to [I]Halo Infinite[/i].

In Escalation Slayer, players progress through a list of weapon and equipment loadouts as they score kills. With each elimination, you advance to a new weapon, culminating in a final challenge to win: getting a kill with the Oddball.

You can also de-level enemy players by meleeing them in the back, so watch your six out there!

The order of loadouts is as follows:
[list][*][b]LEVEL 1[/b]: Rocket Launcher, Cindershot, Repulsor
[*][b]LEVEL 2[/b]: Energy Sword, Gravity Hammer, Grappleshot
[*][b]LEVEL 3[/b]: Sniper Rifle, Skewer, Threat Sensor
[*][b]LEVEL 4[/b]: Hydra, Ravager, Knockback
[*][b]LEVEL 5[/b]: Bulldog, Needler, Grappleshot
[*][b]LEVEL 6[/b]: Battle Rifle, Commando, Threat Sensor
[*][b]LEVEL 7[/b]: Shock Rifle, Stalker Rifle, Drop Wall
[*][b]LEVEL 8[/b]: Heatwave, Sentinel Beam, Evade
[*][b]LEVEL 9[/b]: Bandit, Assault Rifle, Drop Wall
[*][b]LEVEL 10[/b]: Mangler, Sidekick, Threat Sensor
[*][b]LEVEL 11[/b]: Oddball, Shroud[/list]
This mode is launching in Season 3 with two variants: Team Escalation and FFA Escalation.

Team Escalation  progresses all players on a team through the loadout list together. Kills are summed across the team, so everybody’s efforts count. And FFA Escalation  is, of course, every Spartan for themselves!

And yes, there will indeed be a BTB version of Escalation Slayer, along with a “Super” version of the mode which will bring in the special weapon variants and upgraded equipment that you can obtain in [I]Halo Infinite[/i]’s Campaign.

[hr][/hr]
That concludes our showcase of the maps and modes coming when Season 3 of [i]Halo Infinite[/i] launches on March 7.

We can’t wait for you all to embark on a maptacular odyssey that awaits, from the vehicular mosh pit of Oasis, to the dangerous heights of Cliffhanger, and the cavernous depths of Chasm (I don’t know about you, but I was certainly sold the second I heard “Boarding Action with Grappleshots!”)

We’ll be back soon with more information on the Ranked experience and Playlist updates, and follow up with a Sandbox blog as well – so stay tuned for more Season 3 news!

notes.title: Community Collection Playlist Launch
notes.content:
Long before the [i]Halo Infinite[/i] Forge Beta launched with the Winter Update back in November, we knew we were going to have our collective minds blown by the things the community would make and share when we handed over the tools of map and mode creation.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/b3d8b82a2982380d1221ca6e4e6e53646516c09a.jpg[/img]

Three months later, we are still seeing that creativity pushed to new heights every week! 

We delivered the Custom Games Browser to [i]Halo Infinite[/i] ahead of schedule in December, giving you the ability to make every night a custom games night with friends and foes you just haven’t gotten acquainted with yet. 

And now, on the cusp of Season 3, we’re answering the highly requested call to bring community-made Forge maps to their own unique matchmaking playlist. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/40126bb47a33fb439de24801ef20541bbb55ca88.png[/img]

Let’s take a look at what awaits you in the Community Collection playlist, available now!

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Absolution[/h3]
[i][b]Credits[/b]: Anvil Prime 52, Savesme6464, b0b is here
[b]Bookmark[/b]: [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/2182e9f8-7555-4955-874d-1afa6053ea62]Absolution[/url][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/a2256a4e49333c839d3d13e825dccc661f69f464.png[/img]

A map we previously showed off in our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1240440/view/3641753652316265248?l=english]third issue of Forge Features[/url], Absolution has some familiar aspects of a few different maps – from [i]Halo 2[/i]’s Sanctuary to [i]Halo 3[/i]’s Guardian, with that weathered, stone-based Forerunner aesthetic that defined the look of Delta Halo. 

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Perilous[/h3]
[i][b]Credits[/b]: Sikamikanico, Whos Blaze, UnknownEmerald, tdubfed1, Bubba
[b]Bookmark[/b]: [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/5ce22703-8ce9-41a2-976e-db932bd2f2eb]Perilous[/url][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/ae15edb764734bcd5da18f4ef540fd0b69c9778c.jpg[/img]

While not a direct remake of the iconic Lockout from [i]Halo 2[/i], many areas of this map carry elements of that beloved classic that lend a hint of familiarity to this new space.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Salvation[/h3]
[i][b]Credits[/b]: Black Picture, InfiniteForges, Hofsta, tdubfed1
[b]Bookmark[/b]: [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/e1d4a838-d686-4ccb-88b5-02faf2223927]Salvation[/url][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/5bb7d0d40b04c3d31bd26167148e0b78db84738c.jpg[/img]

Damnation from [i]Halo: Combat Evolved[/i] sees a fresh coat of Banished paint and a beautifully revamped industrial aesthetic within a vast cavern. 

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Starboard[/h3]
[i][b]Credits[/b]: Pwn Jones, TheHoodedManZ, The MetaChief, Hitbox unKnown, Max Extra 
[b]Bookmark[/b]: [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/905e7c0b-c453-4a46-a1e6-5f1d375d9529]Starboard[/url][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/099d0a63f357d24ed13407a6b07262f016bf1e0d.jpg[/img]

All hands have been summoned to battle stations on this stunning UNSC-ified spiritual remake of [i]Halo 2[/i]’s Midship.

[hr][/hr]
This is just the beginning for the Community Collection playlist, which will go on to be updated with further community content in the future – we'll have further details to share with you on that front down the road.

notes.title: Yueltidings & Yonder
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/9c3d432902923e678743e3d3b30479e91b86c5ba.png[/img]

Well folks, 2022 is coming to an end and the studio is soon to close its doors for the Holidays. But before we go, I think we’ve got time for one last Community Update to look back on the year just gone – our triumphs, our learnings, our amazing partners, and our pathway into 2023 and beyond...

Let’s get the end-of-year party started with the end-of-year Holiday Community Livestream, where we catch up with various teams around the studio, showcase some Season 3 content for [i]Halo Infinite[/i], and host our final Community Playdate of the year.

[previewyoutube=-lihCw0on1w;full][/previewyoutube]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Halo Infinite[/h2]
[b][i]From Sean Baron, Head of Halo Infinite Live Service[/i][/b]

What a year.

Launching [i]Halo Infinite[/i]’s multiplayer experience on the day we celebrated the franchise’s twentieth anniversary was amazing. Since that day, you have pushed [i]Halo Infinite[/i] to the biggest launch year in the history of the franchise.

In fact, let’s do a quick stats rundown:
[list][*] 170+ million multiplayer matches played
[*] 50+ million campaign missions played
[*] 16+ billion Spartans slayed
[*] 2+ billion bots dispatched
[*] 6 million Spartans “Ninja’d”
[*] 130,000+ maps made in Forge[/list]
(...[i]And a partridge in a pear tree![/i])
 
That’s a whole lot of [i]Halo[/i]!
 
We’re so grateful for the time you’ve spent with us and the passion you have for this franchise. The year has been full of challenges and opportunities.

Yet, your energy and engagement has driven us. We’ve changed the way that we develop and even the way we’re organized. Needless to say, we’re committed to making [i]Halo Infinite[/i] better with every single update!

So, enjoy the rest of the Winter Update. Happy Holidays, and we can’t wait to show you what’s in store for 2023!

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Halo: The Master Chief Collection[/h2]
[b][i]From the MCC team[/i][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/1112d7ccc8036693009d3e6fa93703ceeb436354.jpg[/img]

2022 has been a truly incredible year for MCC!

We said at the start of the year that we had some unfinished business with this title, that we are dedicated to maintaining it with legacy-focused updates to bring in fan-requested features, bug fixes, and new experiences.

Since then, we’ve brought the Flood to [i]Halo 3: ODST[/i]’s Firefight. We’ve given full title support to the Custom Game Browser and mod tools (along with Steam Workshop support and Plug ‘n’ Play); campaign crossplay, customization, and collectibles; Match Rejoin, retroactive Spartan Points, UI updates, new armor sets, and so much more!

We are so grateful for the feedback and support from the fans which has enabled us to close the book on this year on such a high note.

So thank you, happy Halodays, and we’ll catch up with you all in the new year.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]HCS[/h2]
[b][i]From Tashi, Esports Lead[/i][/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/41000caaedada6a156ff22a9fb3073b7d7de3235.jpg[/img]

To say this last year of [i]Halo[/i] esports has been historic would be an understatement, and it’s all thanks to everyone who poured their passion into the scene.

Teams, players, fans, all of our partners, the broadcast talent, and hundreds upon hundreds of staff around the world who busted their butts in support of our mission to deliver epic entertainment to [i]Halo[/i] fans around the world with competition at the core of everything we do. Thank you.

Here are some of the things I’ll cherish from this past year...

[b]Big Team Battle Bonanza 2[/b]: This one of the craziest things we ever tried to pull, and looking back on it I’m so glad we did. It was important that we set the tone for the FUN we wanted fans to have with HCS whether you’re watching in person or at home.  

[b]Different champion for every Major[/b]: A testament to the strength of the scene as well as the balance of the game coming right out the gates at launch. Every tournament has kept us all on the edge of our seats with nonstop surprises and unbelievable plays.

[b]Halo World Championship 2022[/b]: It had been four years since we hosted all of you in Seattle and it was important to us that the event was welcoming to [i]Halo[/i] fans, not just HCS fans. From the Community Stage, to all of our partner activations, to the playable Winter Update build, and of course the amazing tournament – HaloWC 2022 was special no matter how you sliced it. We wished it didn’t have to end!

I’m stopping myself at three because, as I look through our photo gallery, I realize I could probably make a list of 100 things.

[h3]What's Next?[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/13a136eb40e68b42987b8ef13197b80969d5cc7c.png[/img]

Okay, that’s enough of the past, let’s look forward!

We already shared a few details at HaloWC of what to expect. As you may have seen, the OpTic event has been postponed into 2023 and we’ll work closely with OpTic to ensure it lines up nicely with the HCS calendar and that it’s a great event for all fans to attend.

Kicking us off in January, however, is the Spartan Snowdown from the amazing minds at Spacestation. More details to come before the Holidays, but this will be one you don’t want to miss as it’ll be the first competition featuring Argyle and Empyrean, the reimagining of The Pit. Definitely curious to see all of the rosters at that time.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/3a96ec6f6814fed331b0859cc0fb1fdc66c60fc9.jpg[/img]

And, of course, the first Major of 2023 will be in Charlotte, North Carolina from February 24-26 with our partners at Esports Engine. This will be an open event featuring open bracket players from around the world that want to enter, as well as all of the top pro teams back on the mainstage once again for the first time since the Halo World Championship. You can expect VIP and GA tickets and team passes to go on sale in January.

You can also expect the all new HCS Partnered Team Bundles to drop shortly after Charlotte with the launch of Season 3 for [i]Halo Infinite[/i]. The teams have really outdone themselves with the designs and we’ve given them access to a few more tools to be more creative than in Year 1. We can’t for you all to see them!

Later in January, we’re targeting to have the rest of the HCS 2023 roadmap available – as we did last year. We are in the midst of finalizing the roadmap as well as the format updates and we’re looking forward to sharing more in January. Our primary goals are around viewership and participation, and we’re making adjustments to maximize those as best we can.

I can’t understate how monumental of a task it is to put together a full year roadmap, particularly when we were just traveling around the world running the first year of [i]Halo Infinite[/i] esports at the same time. In some ways, it’s been more challenging than before the game launched. We are committed to the long-term sustainability of the scene and we want fans and players to be able to plan out their entire year ahead of time.

On the topic of maps, modes, and settings – you can expect to see the full list of map/mode combinations in the New Year, as well as some updates to settings on Argyle and Empyrean based on player feedback. Additionally, the studio is working on a balance update to land just before Charlotte to further refine competitive play just before the big event. Look for more specifics in early January. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/e38484593bdb7f328273a67b6c00a4bd62b1d345.jpg[/img]

Finally, I want to give thanks to the rest of the HCS Team who have gone above and beyond all year long to make this all happen for the community. We’re a small team, but we pack a punch!

(Yes, I got us all matching hoodies just for our team!)

Thank you – happy Holidays and happy new year!

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Halo Gear[/h2]
[i][b]From Megan Castro, Marketing Manager, Halo Consumer Products[/b][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/3ee6dc5dcf0bb6f24765832c7ba108dec62e60c8.png[/img]

It’s hard to believe we’re nearing the end of another amazing year of [i]Halo[/i], but time flies when you’re having fun.

For the Halo Gear team, this year has been filled with incredible partnerships, programs, and amazing product releases. In 2022, we continued to build on our long-term partnerships, began new ones, expanded into more categories through unique collaborations, and we tried something new in the Halo Gear Shop with the Halo Gear Rewards program – where players can earn physical rewards from playing [i]Halo[/i].
 
This year we released many amazing Halo products, and we’ll highlight a few here that are sure to bring joy to the Halo fan in your life this Holiday season.

Just released, comes the next drop from our partnership with Wolverine – the [i]Halo[/i] Spartan Boots are inspired by armors from the [i]Halo Infinite[/i] multiplayer experience. [url=https://www.wolverine.com/US/en/halo-spartan-boot/54562M.html]The Green Camo boot is now available[/url]! Stay tuned for more drops from Wolverine x [i]Halo[/i] coming in Spring 2023.

That’s so metal, [i]Halo[/i] Metal Posters! [url=https://displate.com/licensed/halo-game]Adorn your walls with these metal posters from Displate[/url], featuring new graphic artwork of the Master Chief, the Weapon, Halo Insignia, vehicles, and more.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/317ba801d058a6bcd0105364412b28fc2ccbb099.jpg[/img]

Let’s ride! [url=https://www.walmart.com/ip/24-Volt-Microsoft-Halo-Warthog-Ride-On-with-Laser-Tag-Blaster-and-Vest-Included-For-Boys-Girls-Ages-3-and-up/783754636?athbdg=L1100]Get up to 9MPH on the [i]Halo[/i] Warthog Electric Ride On[/url]. This drivable Warthog comes with working lights, sounds, moveable Gauss Cannon, and laser tag vest and blaster – available now only at Walmart.

In collaboration with Haworth comes [url=https://store.haworth.com/pages/halo-legendary]the Haworth x [i]Halo[/i]: Fern Gaming Chair[/url]. This premium ergonomic chair is precision engineered to provide maximum comfort for hours of work and play. Perfect for the home office that doubles as the gaming room. #ComfortEvolved

In collaboration with Adidas Originals, [url=https://www.adidas.com/us/nmd]we created the [i]Halo Infinite[/i] Adidas NMD V3[/url], and Adidas classic meets Halo with design inspired by the AI characters in the [i]Halo Infinite[/i] multiplayer experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/f07a74bdc8ee083790427566119d221c3204018d.png[/img]

[url=https://gear.xbox.com/products/halo-the-official-cookbook]For the foodies, this year we welcomed [i]Halo: The Official Cookbook[/i][/url]! Authored by Victoria Rosenthal, this massive cookbook has over 70 recipes with step-by-step instructions and photos to create these [i]Halo[/i]-inspired foods at home. Level up this gift with [url=https://gear.xbox.com/collections/halo/products/halo-master-chief-117-scorcher-8pc-stoneware-dinner-set]the Master Chief 117 dinnerware set from Ukonic, available in the Halo Gear Shop[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/245d941f0b7de39a4c0cc0ac3ba6bcbfccead7f3.jpg[/img]

Mega Construx released the massive UNSC Forward Unto Dawn collector building set, complete with a Miranda Keyes micro action figure and display stand – [url=https://www.target.com/p/mega-halo-unsc-forward-unto-dawn-navy-ship-building-set-680pcs/-/A-84799735#lnk=sametab]available exclusively at Target[/url].

Dark Horse Comics delivered two incredible [i]Halo[/i] statues this year: the [url=https://www.darkhorse.com/Products/3010-736/Halo-Infinite-Spartan-Yoroi-PVC-Statue]Spartan Yoroi[/url] and [url=https://gear.xbox.com/collections/halo/products/halo-infinite-spartan-yoroi-xgs-exclusive-statue]Spartan Chonmage/Yokai[/url] (Halo Gear Shop Exclusive), featuring the formidable Spartans from the [i]Halo Infinite[/i] multiplayer event Fracture: Tenrai. A great collector’s piece.
 
From Jazwares, the Master Chief Deluxe helmet with working lights, sounds, and VO from the Chief himself, and the highly detailed figures of the 6-inch Spartan Collection and 4-inch World of Halo lines are the perfect addition to a Halo collection. [url=https://www.gamestop.com/search/?q=Halo%20Jazwares&type=Primary&sort=BestMatch_Desc&p=1&lang=default]Find [i]Halo[/i] Jazwares products at GameStop and other major retailers[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/c3ff9dc5c08d1b097a4e12f59b6398b2d463446f.jpg[/img]

For the lore-lovers, return to Zeta Halo and dive deeper into the universe with [url=https://www.simonandschuster.com/books/Halo-The-Rubicon-Protocol/Kelly-Gay/Halo/9781982147884]the latest novel from Kelly Gay, [i]Halo: The Rubicon Protocol[/i][/url].

We’re proud to work with our costume partner Disguise Costumes to create and release the first adaptive costumes for children with accessibility challenges, [url=https://www.amazon.com/Master-Infinite-Adaptive-Costume-Medium/dp/B09BRRZW1Z/ref=sr_1_2?crid=BBOYHI98TZBQ&keywords=Disguise%2BHalo%2BInfinite%2Badaptive%2Bcostume&qid=1670540673&sprefix=disguise%2Bhalo%2Binfinite%2Badaptive%2Bcostume%2Caps%2C112&sr=8-2&th=1]a Master Chief costume with mask[/url] and Warthog wheelchair cover.

[b][url=https://gear.xbox.com/pages/halo]Be sure to visit the Halo Gear Shop[/url][/b] – your one stop shop for all things [i]Halo[/i] including, exclusive apparel such as the [i]Halo[/i] x Action Figure Miles collection, seasonal [i]Halo[/i] styles, HCS Gear, collectibles such as the Spartan Chonmage/Yokai statue from Dark Horse Comics, housewares, novels, jewelry, and more!

Stay tuned to [url=https://twitter.com/HaloGear]@HaloGear[/url] on social for all the latest news and updates.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Partnerships[/h2]
[i][b]From Katie Jerauld, Sr. Marketing Manager, Brand Partnerships Lead[/b][/i]

2022 might not have been a launch year for [i]Halo[/i], but that didn’t stop us from launching huge, hilarious, and h…impactful partnerships.

As the year draws to a close, we wanted to share some exciting 2022 [i]Halo[/i] partnership highlights, remind you all of programs you can still participate in, and round it out with an update on our newest program to get you through the Holidays:

[h3]Awards![/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/83f9f339e61b1562b623615a909ebd7a69efdb76.jpg[/img]

In 2022, we saw some awards come in for previous programs, and like a proud parent, I couldn’t let the end-of-year blog slip by without sharing that the OPI x Xbox program (which featured a [i]Halo[/i]-themed nail color as well as matching armor coating) [url=https://clios.com/entertainment/winner/games-partnerships-collaborations-campaign/microsoft-xbox/xbox-opi-125127]won a Clio award in the "Partnerships & Collaborations Campaign" category[/url].

Our 2021 Swarovski x [i]Halo[/i] partnership also [url=https://www.reggieawards.org/a/gallery/rounds/43/details/14084]won a Gold Reggie for the beautiful 20th Anniversary collectables we created together[/url]. We love it when we get a glimpse of a crystal helmet in the background of a stream, and to see the sparkly Spartans in the OPI coatings that are still present in almost every MP match.

[h3]Trolli[/h3]
We're partnered through the end of this year with the delightfully dark brand. [url=https://twitter.com/Trolli_USA/status/1583186443374981121?s=20&t=6YYpoNo3D18RgThT_z4CFQ]Let us [i]never[/i] forget the Feedler[/url], the booth at the [url=https://twitter.com/Trolli_USA/status/1584016535466971136?s=20&t=LVUtn-RV7iYA8lpnmRclcA]HCS World Championship[/url], the [url=https://twitter.com/Trolli_USA/status/1577411415530299392?s=20&t=1c6zmJ6ri0tRw9wqeT0U-g]Hunter made out of Trolli gummies[/url] (because how could we not?), and last but not least please let us not forget Sketch living his (and our) glorious gummy dreams.

([url=https://twitter.com/Halo/status/1584279572123881472?s=20&t=6YYpoNo3D18RgThT_z4CFQ]We will take any opportunity to remind people of this glorious video[/url]!)

[url=https://www.trolli.com/halo]You can still enter to win a Trolli Ultimate Gaming Bundle[/url] and you’ll still find the 4 collectable [i]Halo[/i]-themed packs with 2XP and Challenge Swaps in stores though the end of this year!

[url=https://gear.xbox.com/products/halo-halo-trol-adult-short-sleeve-t-shirt]And we would be remiss if we did not shamelessly plug the limited edition Feedler tee[/url]. It would be a great stocking stuffer for the family Troll…..i fan.

[h3]Rockstar & Doritos[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/72bea73d86c055af7ef0a986b9d4770a7e4e1c7f.jpg[/img]

Master Chief is still on Rockstar cans and Doritos bags around the world as part of [url=https://www.doritosrockstarenergy.com/home]the Xbox partnership with Rockstar and Doritos[/url]. In some regions, fans can even get their hands on the 2022 Tasteful Sensation Razorback coating.

(*slaps roof of Razorback*) This bad boy can fit so many Spartans in it!

[h3]Honda Fan Cup Tournament[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/93ec543867f4a036c7dc4124a86a3b78001915bf.png[/img]

We're in the home stretch of the Honda Fan Cup Tournament featuring [i]Halo Infinite[/i]. There’s just one qualifier left – on December 18.

It’s not too late to show off your skills and take a shot at the massive $20,000 prize pool. In addition to the prize money, the top finisher in the Finals will win an exclusive Haworth x [i]Halo[/i] Fern Gaming Chair.

[url=https://www.start.gg/league/honda-fan-cup-1/details]Register now[/url], and we hope you’ll tune in to watch the Finals, which will be livestreamed on the Xbox Twitch channel on January 7 at 11am PT.

[h3]Calm[/h3]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/27375063f740cf5e96517e375a45492047d094d6.jpg[/img]

Just in time to round out the year and support your mental health during the Holidays, Xbox has partnered with Calm – the #1 app for sleep, meditation and relaxation – to bring the first-ever video game-themed soundscapes to the platform.

We've created a soundscape that takes you on a relaxing ambient journey through Zeta Halo, and players can also enjoy a soothing soundscape from [i]Sea of Thieves[/i], both available on Calm Premium.

[url=https://www.calm.com/app/program/VWlNO11cnQ]Listen to the calming soundscapes of Zeta Halo here[/url]!

To ensure players can listen to the new soundscapes with ease, Xbox and Calm are offering an Xbox Game Pass Ultimate Perk, where Ultimate members can receive three months of Calm Premium for free, and then 50% off their first-year subscription for new Calm Premium members. Those who aren’t yet Ultimate members can take advantage of Calm's 7-day free trial to Calm Premium.

The partnership with Calm is part of Xbox’s ongoing commitment to supporting players’ mental health and connecting them with resources to support their well-being. Learn more here.

We hope you’re able to snack, play, listen and relax this Holiday season, and see you in 2023!

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Halo the Series[/h2]
[i][b]From Cheryl Marine, Sr. Transmedia Producer[/b][/i]

[i]Halo The Series – Special Collector’s Edition[/i], now available for the Holiday!

Season 1 has just released on DVD, Blu-Ray, including a Limited Edition Steelbook that makes for a great collectible.

[quote][i]In a war for humanity's survival, our deadliest weapon is our greatest hope. Master Chief, Cortana, the Covenant, and the Spartans of Silver Team weave a personal story with action, adventure and a richly imagined vision of the future.

The series, currently streaming on Paramount+, stars Pablo Schreiber (Master Chief, John-117), Natascha McElhone (Dr. Halsey), Jen Taylor (Cortana), Bokeem Woodbine (Soren-066), and is produced by SHOWTIME® in partnership with 343 Industries, along with Amblin Television.[/i][/quote]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/30d33a5034871e36ed6f7abd22b57df7cd8f0aca.png[/img]

The special 5-disc collection features the complete season – that’s all nine episodes at 4k quality – plus more than five hours of behind-the-scenes special features, including 75 minutes of exclusive content that takes you beyond the screen, providing a deeper look into the world of [i]Halo[/i]. The cast and crew share their experiences creating the worlds, characters, costumes, and props that helped bring Halo to life on such a massive scale.

Also included are all nine episodes of the companion series [i]Halo The Series: Declassified[/i], a premium case, and collectible art cards of Master Chief, Silver Team, Dr. Halsey, and other favorite characters from the show.

This collectible Steelbook is perfect for the [i]Halo[/i] fan on your Holiday gift list to see an even more in-depth look at the [i]Halo[/i] television series. [url=https://www.amazon.com/Halo-Season-Limited-Edtion-Steelbook/dp/B0BF2WXJ3X/ref=sr_1_1?crid=160MFOZXQL9YP&keywords=B0BF2WXJ3X&qid=1668047000&sprefix=b0bf2wxj3x%2Caps%2C161&sr=8-1]You can order your collectable Steelbook here[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/61af8f35abfac95b5eb5268ffe6882342e35faf1.png[/img]
 
We have other options too. If you’d like it on DVD, Blu-ray, or 4K Ultra HD, those are also available at Amazon and other retailers. [url=https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/store/b/HaloOriginalSeries]And a digital download is available from the Microsoft Store[/url].

And, in case you missed it, Silver Team is back in production filming season 2 in Iceland and Budapest. We hope to bring you more details about the series in the new year.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/14e46d43c49a4ed11f617053e8ccad698881736a.jpg[/img]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]The Artist's Corner[/h2]

Our final Artist’s Corner piece from [url=https://gear.xbox.com/products/halo-mythos][i]Halo Mythos[/i][/url] for this year comes from Jean-Sébastien Rossbach, depicting the Spartan-IIs.

With no end to humanity’s civil war – the Insurrection – in sight, its outcome looking increasingly grim, Dr. Catherine Halsey initiated the SPARTAN-II program.

This saw the full-scale production of biologically-augmented, armor-enhanced super-soldiers. Their origins, however, cast a dark shadow on these living legends, as they were kidnapped as children and replaced by genetically defective flash clones. The candidates were put through torturous training exercises from the age of six, and many would not survive the augmentation procedures that reforged their bodies into the UNSC’s most powerful weapons of war.

But it is their actions which inspire hope amongst those who have seen them in action, or heard the stories passed between fellow soldiers about armored super-soldiers who were able to turn the tide against their unstoppable alien foes. And the Covenant would come to know these Spartans by their own name – [i]demons[/i].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/668f818b55ab3fdddb25e4fdd02198abed32587e.png[/img]
[i][url=https://wpassets.halowaypoint.com/wp-content/2022/12/Mythos-Spartan-IIs-Jean-Sebastien-Rossbach.jpg]Grab a high-res copy for yourself right here![/url][/i]

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Fin[/h2]

That’s a wrap for us this year! It’s been a hell of a ride and we’re flooring the accelerator when Season 3 (“Echoes Within”) arrives in 2023 as we look forwards to more regular content drops and updates for [i]Halo Infinite[/i]... but, for now, let’s pump the brakes and enjoy the Holiday break with our loved ones.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/9a5191aa8b1992b6f075723e4d82a9ce2bfa6422.jpg[/img]
[i][url=https://wpassets.halowaypoint.com/wp-content/2022/12/2022_1208_Internal_HolidayCard_4k-scaled.jpg]Download a 4K copy from here[/url]![/i]

We have, of course, got the Winter Contingency II event launching next week which will feature a free Event Pass consisting of ten new Holiday-themed cosmetics – including a particularly festive helmet attachment that I certainly can’t wait to rock in matchmaking! You can definitely expect to see a launch blog for that to cover all the details on Tuesday.

Otherwise, be well, be merry, be kind and good to each other. Thank you for all your support over the course of this year, we can’t wait to share our plans for the future with you.

See you in 2023!

notes.title: December Update
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/732fa1826716853d4e3f6fd6cffdf5cfc8eb2941.jpg[/img]

In the spirit of the Holiday season, how about some early presents for [i]Halo Infinite[/i]? 

On the heels of the Winter Update, which launched just last month, we’re tremendously excited to deliver our latest game update for [i]Halo Infinite[/i] which brings with it some brand new features and a variety of key improvements to the game experience. 

The team has been working hard on addressing player feedback, and so – before we break for the Holidays – we’re bringing you a new (yet familiar) map, free armor cores and coatings, some quality-of-life improvements, and the early release of the Custom Games Browser… 

The latest update is available now, for free, on Xbox and PC. So, let’s talk a little bit more about what’s just arrived! 

[previewyoutube=bTjL_AMaWns;full][/previewyoutube]

[url=https://aka.ms/HaloInfiniteUpdate]Visit the Halo Support site to review the official patch notes[/url].

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Custom Game Browser[/h2]

Since the release of the Forge Beta with the Winter Update, just a month ago, the floodgates have well and truly opened to a barrage of incredible community-created maps and modes. For a look at some of our favorites, be sure to check out our Forge Features blog series! 
 
Of course, in order to unlock the true potential of Forge and make these wonderfully unique experiences (which have long been such a definitive aspect of [i]Halo[/i]) more accessible to everyone, we’re excited to announce that [b]we’re debuting the V1 of the Custom Game Browser today[/b] – months ahead of our original target! 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/8b8ac4935063d54a4b65032bb34211df17e2b2a1.jpg[/img]
 
Previously scheduled to release in Season 3, we fully agree with players who felt that the Custom Game Browser should be a priority – it’s a key support structure for what players create in Forge and a pillar for the community. The team worked incredibly hard to land this feature so much further in advance, but with that comes the caveat that this is a “V1.” It is therefore likely to have some rough edges, but we felt it was more important that we get this in the hands of players sooner rather than later. The CGB will, of course, continue to evolve with support over time. 

For more information, including instructions on how the CGB works, please refer to this article on the Halo Support site. 

Give us your feedback here and [url=https://aka.ms/HaloSupport]be sure to report any bugs and issues on Halo Support[/url]. 

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Enter Empyrean[/h2]

The Pit has come to [i]Halo Infinite[/i]!

This beloved map from [i]Halo 3[/i] has been officially rebuilt in Forge by the 343 Industries team and is now reborn as Empyrean. 

Empyrean is a reimagining of The Pit, complete with some refreshed aesthetics over its familiar layout, and no expense spared on attention to detail. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/500d674ef65c8fc8a4a8cdfa4ce0a21d77a3e132.png[/img]

For those of you familiar with The Pit (or even its [i]Halo 4[/i] incarnation, Pitfall), you already know the dance. The immediate rush to grab the rocket launcher, the sniper duels atop its two opposing towers, the potential close-quarters perils of the control room – but this time, there are some new notes to be added to this symphony as it comes with the additional layer of [i]Halo Infinite[/i]’s gameplay and sandbox features. 

How do [i]Halo Infinite[/i]’s toys, like its limited-use Equipment, alter some of those dynamics and affect how you traverse the combat dance floor? Maybe the enemy team managed to grab the rockets first, but you went and acquired the Repulsor to protect yourself (and hopefully your teammates as well). We can’t wait to see what new memories are forged in this proving ground! 

Empyrean is available now in Matchmaking and Custom Games. 

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Complimentary Cosmetics[/h2]

Over the last year, we’ve received a lot of feedback around [i]Halo Infinite[/i]’s armor customization, and we are keenly aware that players – both new and returning – may have missed out on some unique content from over the course of Seasons 1 and 2. 

We want to ensure that all players have a suite of customization options open to them from the get-go, and as a result of that feedback we are hoping that this update opens a number of those doors. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/9a9e739a78216a9da3e67acfd9f63daff14752a9.jpg[/img]

[list][*][b]All present Armor Cores are now available to all players[/b]. This means that all players now possess the Mark VII, Mark V (B), RAKSHASA, YOROI, and EAGLESTRIKE Armor Cores for free
[*][b]All 10 Cadet Coatings have been added to existing Armor Cores[/b]. Similar to the above, each Armor Core now has a starting suite of 10 Cadet Coatings – this includes the non-default Cores, and they will also be included with all future Cores[/list]
Variety, as they say, is the spice of life, and we hope that having these options as the bedrock of customization in [i]Halo Infinite[/i] provides players more options to outfit their Spartan to their liking. 

Simply log into [i]Halo Infinite[/i] and these Cores 'n' Coatings will be automatically added to your cosmetic inventory. 

Visit the Armor Hall today to explore these updated customization options! 

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Quality of Life Improvements[/h2]

As we continue to support [i]Halo Infinite[/i], we have been working to bring various fixes and improvements across the title which are directly aimed at addressing key areas of player feedback. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/36fa8055c2f97ccf4a6db5327172b9af2cd77d66.jpg[/img]

Here are a few notable callouts that have come with this update… 

[list][*] [b]Mouse & Keyboard[/b]: Improvements have been made to mouse and keyboard input. This includes aiming improvements, enabling red reticle, adding a walk button (which has its own suite of custom options around speed and hold/toggle), and improvements have also been made to the mouse scroll wheel input
[*] [b]Networking & Desync[/b]: Improvements have been made to networking, which should reduce instances of “desync.” Vehicles desycning, melee attacks not registering, and blank shots (due to fake reloads) should all see improvements with this update
[*] [b]Player reporting[/b]: In-game player reporting has been added to the scoreboard (accessed during a match by pressing the Back button) and post-game carnage report. Players can also be muted from the Back button scoreboard
[*] [b]Sandbox updates[/b]: Melee clang logic for the Energy Sword has also been updated—if both players have no shields and melee each other, both players will now trade melees and die in order to prevent the Energy Sword from tearing through teams without trading[url=https://steamcommunity.com/games/1240440/announcements/detail/3398556047593672385]Check out the details in our previous Sandbox blog[/url][/list]
[url=https://aka.ms/HaloInfiniteUpdate]Find the full patch notes on Halo Support[/url]. 

[hr][/hr]
[H2]Thank You![/h2]

The last thing we want to say to close this update out is thank you! 

Thank you to all our players who continue to provide us with feedback that enables us to continue supporting [i]Halo Infinite[/i], forging it into a better experience as we move forwards. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/f38b6fc8f542938bbb3880771f03063da798f6a9.jpg[/img]

This first year of [i]Halo Infinite[/i] has been one of many tough lessons learned, but we are confident that we are turning that corner in 2023 as we look forward to delivering Season 3 and more – more content, more features and options, more weapons, more cosmetics, more updates – on a regular cadence that keeps the Halo hype rolling all year long. 

In the meantime, be sure to hop into [i]Halo Infinite[/i] to check out the Winter Update. This free content update brought with it Campaign Network Co-Op and Mission Replay alongside some new Achievements, the Forge Beta, a free 30-tier Battle Pass, new maps, a new mode, and we’ve got two free new events as well (Winter Contingency 2 in December and Joint Fire in January). 

We’re excited to continue taking these positive steps forward together, and on behalf of the entire 343 Industries team we hope you have a wonderful Holiday season. If you're interested in the press kit, [url=https://aka.ms/DecemberUpdatePressKit]you can grab a copy for yourself from here[/url]!

See you in 2023!

- All present Armor Cores are now available to all players. This means that all players now possess the Mark VII, Mark V (B), RAKSHASA, YOROI, and EAGLESTRIKE Armor Cores for free

- All 10 Cadet Coatings have been added to existing Armor Cores. Similar to the above, each Armor Core now has a starting suite of 10 Cadet Coatings – this includes the non-default Cores, and they will also be included with all future Cores

- Player reporting: In-game player reporting has been added to the scoreboard (accessed during a match by pressing the Back button) and post-game carnage report. Players can also be muted from the Back button scoreboard

tags.bug: - Networking & Desync: Improvements have been made to networking, which should reduce instances of “desync.” Vehicles desycning, melee attacks not registering, and blank shots (due to fake reloads) should all see improvements with this update

tags.balance_change: - Sandbox updates: Melee clang logic for the Energy Sword has also been updated—if both players have no shields and melee each other, both players will now trade melees and die in order to prevent the Energy Sword from tearing through teams without trading

notes.title: Forge Features
notes.content:
Forge has come to [i]Halo Infinite[/i]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/2846a902d8a97f587425eef885a8864400720b3a.jpg[/img]

First introduced in [i]Halo[/i] 3 all the way back in 2007, this feature has evolved from its original intent to serve as a map editor for moving spawns, replacing weapons, and adding geometry, to become something else altogether.

The reason for that lies in the community. You used teleporter nodes to suspend crates in the air on Last Resort. You took weapons, grenades, and respawn points, made makeshift visual effects in certain rooms, and made iconic screenshot art. And you learned tricks like “interlocking” and “geomerging,” combining objects together and phasing them through the environment, to not only edit existing maps but create brand new ones.

And that was just the beginning. In each successive instalment with Forge, the goal has been to empower players with these abilities as tools at their disposal, which has culminated in where we are today. In 2022, Forge is more powerful than ever before and in the last week that it’s been added to [i]Halo Infinite[/i] as part of the Winter Update, we’ve already seen the community’s creative spirit begin to flourish.

That means the time has come for a “Forge Spotlight,” a new monthly blog feature where we bring some of the coolest community-made content your way.

With advancement naturally comes a certain feeling of intimidation and fear over a loss of comfortable, learned simplicity. There’s so much you can do that it can feel difficult to know where to start, and so this series is designed to say... start here! Try out the things that folks in the community are making, and let’s give you the tutorials and insights that will set you on your own odyssey with Forge.

[hr][/hr]
[h2]Maps & Modes[/h2]

Let’s take a look at some awesome maps that you can find and bookmark right now via the Content Browser!

[h3]Paintball[/h3]
[i]Credits: Map by Mabel Tree, mode by b0b is here[/i]
[i]Bookmark: [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/d0de44a3-7dca-4a0c-aaef-217f7056c0cb]Paintball Map[/url] | [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/d0de44a3-7dca-4a0c-aaef-217f7056c0cb]Paintball Game Mode[/url][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/cc8b7f75b96eef37c11feaaabbfd629f67fc701f.jpg[/img]

I remember the first time I played Paintball in [i]Halo 3[/i]. Back in ‘08, it was instant kill Plasma Pistols on a Forged map on Foundry, and I lost many hours to it with friends.

With the Forge Beta in [i]Halo Infinite[/i], Paintball returns! “Weapon combination” through scripting enables you to wield a Battle Rifle that shoots plasma bolts from a Pulse Carbine while your Sidekick fires Plasma Pistol bolts.

With jumping disabled, Paintball is all about how you use the various objects and structures of the map for cover while anticipating the movement of your enemies.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Repulsoccer[/h3]
[i]Credits: b0b is here, unsorted guy[/i]
[i]Bookmark: [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/695e1a86-56e2-490c-9a2c-dc03b0d58fee]Repulsoccer Desert[/url] | [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/modes/9a76a6ac-8393-46a5-8045-963489f14fa6]Repulsoccer Game Mode[/url][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/e0aa9573f7c82c134eefcb4dccb6c7e8b8390704.jpg[/img]

In the past, we’ve been able to create goals and hit a ball around with Gravity Hammers, but Repulsoccer takes things to a whole new level!

Using the Repulsor equipment, two teams can move an energy ball around the map with the aim of getting it into the enemy’s goal. If the energy ball touches you, you’re dead and have to wait to respawn – of course, you can help thin the numbers of the enemy team with your Energy Sword as well.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Haven[/h3]
[i]Credits: DarkMaiming, Corbman[/i]
[i]Bookmark: [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/674c14f5-1b40-4358-916e-bc45c663b996]Haven[/url][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/969d16dba21ac9d743daed75683968acba7145c4.jpg[/img]

A fan-favorite classic from [i]Halo 4[/i]’s multiplayer, Haven has been rebuilt in [i]Halo Infinite[/i].

Haven has everything there is to love about a [i]Halo[/i] multiplayer map – it's a Forerunner-themed symmetrical arena map capable of hosting a broad variety of modes for some great 4v4 action.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Coagulation[/h3]
[i]Credits: AlphaEpsilon, BicyclicHealer2[/i]
[i]Bookmark: [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/d75e5607-346a-432c-a542-ecb6f5d2643b]Coagulation[/url][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/b15eb57390eaec1a2811fb0a2f8dda12b2fdf858.jpg[/img]

Speaking of fan-favorite classics, it is only natural that, upon getting a tool like Forge in their hands, the community would remake this map in particular—and that’s exactly what BicyclicHealer2 and the fittingly-named AlphaEpsilon have done.

Named Coagulation after the [i]Halo 2[/i] incarnation of this unforgettable boxed-in canyon, the map itself is actually a recreation of the original Blood Gulch we know and love.

Grab some friends and contemplate life's great mysteries about why we’re here... or blow each other up with tanks. Either’s good!

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Valhalla[/h3]
[i]Credits: DarthPepper, Chewbaci, anakin53106[/i]
[i]Bookmark: [url=https://www.halowaypoint.com/halo-infinite/ugc/maps/36e8b0a2-c994-4eff-ae6a-19382b618324]Valhalla[/url][/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/38365036/0ba7cdd773df9cb24e799a088eddda12428b2163.jpg[/img]

[i]Halo 3[/i] gave us a spiritual remake of Coagulation in the form of Valhalla, and this recreation of the map by DarthPepper, Chewbaci, and anakin53106 (that’s a lot of Anakins!) is a fantastic first go at bringing this beloved space to [i]Halo Infinite[/i].

As a co-Forged map, it’s amazing to see what kind of community content can come from a group of people pooling their memories of the series with the collective creative talent they have for utilizing Forge as a tool.

[hr][/hr]
[h3]Community Creations[/h3]

As a critical aspect of the [i]Halo[/i] franchise, some of you may be wondering where you can find and connect with the Forge community. Two of the core places you should definitely check out are:

[list][*] [url=https://www.forgehub.com/]ForgeHub[/url]
[*] [url=https://forge.xboxera.com/]Forgera[/url][/list]
Here, you’ll find lively forums for discussion and sharing, detailed browsers for maps, news and updates, and much more! And you can always hit up [url=https://discord.gg/Halo]the official Halo Discord[/url] if you’re looking for people to play with.

Of course, we’re not the only ones highlighting Forge maps and modes, which brings us to some of the guides and tutorials for Forge made by the community for the community.

First up, Red Nomster has been putting together some great tutorial guides on how to use Forge.

In his first part, Red Nomster looks at how to get started in Forge – from simple things like placing objects and examining their properties, to getting you started on the fundamentals of FX tricks, and how to weld and script a door.

[previewyoutube=PX6tVg5e9xU;full][/previewyoutube]

The second part takes a closer look at how you can Forge interactive maps in [i]Halo Infinite[/i], implementing features like double and automatic doors, elevators, and ladders.

[previewyoutube=m3u7XaHU47k;full][/previewyoutube]

DEWtheMCCOY has been rounding up various Forge maps from the community to show them off each day since the Winter Update launch. We applaud this incredible dedication, and you should definitely keep up with this showcase of amazing content!

[previewyoutube=v8Z4LS4wsjA;full][/previewyoutube]

Our own [url=https://twitter.com/DvsSound]Senior Sound Designer Robbie Elias[/url] has been putting together some videos that show some of the cool things you can do with scripting nodegraphs in Forge.

Remember in [i]Halo 2[/i]’s Cairo Station and [i]Halo 4[/i]’s Dawn when you go out the airlocks for a spacewalk and the audio changes to muffle the sound effects? You can set that up as a global audio effect, which means it’s time for y’all to leverage this for a truly immersive Boarding Action remake!

[list][*][url=https://twitter.com/DvsSound/status/1590330785768562692]How to set global audio[/url]
[*][url=https://twitter.com/DvsSound/status/1590342974009135104]Using node graphs to trigger sounds on specific objects when specific events happen[/url]
[*][url=https://twitter.com/DvsSound/status/1590335226215305216]Changing what different players/teams hear[/url]
[*][url=https://twitter.com/DvsSound/status/1590348204184604674]Using node graphs to stop doors moving/opening sound when interacting with terminals[/url][/list]
[hr][/hr]

With that, we bring our first Forge Feature to an end!

This is just the beginning of incredibly exciting things to come with Forge – both in terms of continuing to build on the mode and in seeing what creations of yours will continue to amaze and astound us. We couldn’t be more excited to be embarking on this Great Journey with you.

Looking to give us feedback on Forge? Leave it here on Steam or head over to our [url=https://forums.halowaypoint.com/t/official-forge-fedback-thread/553696]Forge Feedback thread on the Halo Waypoint forums[/url] and let us know your thoughts.

Also, while sharing your Forge content online, just like with other community creations, be sure to tag it with #HaloSpotlight!

To end this first Forge Features blog with a question: 

What’s your favorite Forge creation you’ve seen so far? Let us know!
